DAMGHANI:v1p218/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r1.claim: Tazakkā can mean to reform or make oneself upright.
DAMGHANI:v1p218/r1.anchor: قوله سبحانه في سورة فاطر " ومن تزكى " يعني أصلح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r2.claim: A report says al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra told believers to disbelieve in Muḥammad and let him bear their burden; the verse was revealed in response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r2.anchor: روي أن الوليد بن المغيرة قال لقوم من المؤمنين: اكفروا بمحمد وعلي وزركم، فنزلت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Qatāda say the verse concerns sins and crimes: no soul is punished for another's sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة: هذه الآية في الذنوب والجرائم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r4.claim: وازرة abbreviates نفس وازرة; the point is that each soul carries only its own load, unlike earthly tyrants who punish associates and relatives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r4.anchor: ووازرة: صفة لمحذوف، أي نفس وازرة: حاملة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says rulers who punish a criminal's relative act unjustly unless the relative aided, supported, or knowingly approved the crime and thus shared responsibility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ومن تطرف من الحكام إلى أخذ قريب بقريبه في جريمة، كفعل زياد ونحوه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r6.claim: The verse does not conflict with the passage in al-ʿAnkabūt: misleaders bear the burden of their own misguidance as well as the consequences of misleading others, never another person's burden itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r6.anchor: ولا منافاة بين هذه الآية والتي في العنكبوت، لأن تلك في الضالين المضلين يحملون أثقال إضلال الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r7.claim: A burdened soul receives no aid even from a close relative; the next clause stresses the denial of help, extending the image of a load carried on the back to sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p23#2/r7.anchor: وإن تدع مثقلة: أي نفس مثقلة بحملها، إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء: أي لا غياث يومئذ لمن استغاث،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī leaves the called person implicit so the wording includes every possible helper; the pronoun in كان refers to that understood person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r1.anchor: قال: وترك المدعو ليعم ويشمل كل مدعو.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes كان as 'were' with an omitted subject: even if the caller were a close relative of the person appealed to, no burden would be lifted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: واسم كان مضمر تقديره ولو كان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r3.claim: The feminine form مثقلة refers generically to a person, so the following pronoun can be masculine by sense; a transmitted reading also has كان ذو قربى as a complete verb meaning 'were present'.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r3.anchor: وذكر الضمير حملا على المعنى، لأن قوله: مثقلة، لا يريد به مؤنث المعنى فقط، بل كل شخص،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī prefers the incomplete-verb parsing because it fits the sense that a burdened soul's relative cannot carry its load; Abū Ḥayyān says his alternative is coherent too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: نظم الكلام أحسن ملاءمة للناقصة، لأن المعنى:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r6.claim: Most readers have ومن تزكى / يتزكى; al-ʿAbbās from Abū ʿAmr assimilates the tāʾ into zāy, while Ibn Masʿūd and Ṭalḥa also assimilate it with a hamzat al-waṣl in the initial form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p24/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ومن تزكى، فعلا ماضيا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r2.claim: Wealth, children, and lifespan are God's gifts and control; cosmic harmony shows that an all-powerful sustaining God governs, while other deities can neither govern nor help at judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r2.anchor: The harmony found in the conflicting elements of this universe clearly shows that it is being governed by the all-powerful and sustaining God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r3.claim: Ignoring the truth harms people rather than God, who does not need them; the Prophet's preaching reaches living hearts, while the dead-hearted face their ordained fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p324/r3.anchor: God does not need them; it is they who need Him.

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r1.claim: وازرة means a burden-bearing soul, with نفس omitted as understood; تزر means bears, so no soul bears another's burden.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r1.anchor: قوله: { وازرة }: أي: نفس وازرة، فحذف الموصوف للعلم [به]. ومعنى تزر: تحمل

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r2.claim: A soul weighed by sins calls another soul to carry its load; the called object is omitted as understood.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r2.anchor: قوله: { وإن تدع مثقلة } أي: نفس مثقلة بالذنوب نفسا إلى حملها. فحذف المفعول به للعلم به.

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r3.claim: The common passive reading makes شيء the deputy subject.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r3.anchor: والعامة " لا يحمل " مبنيا للمفعول و " شيء " قائم مقام فاعله.

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r4.speaker: أبو السمال وطلحة
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r4.claim: Abu al-Simal and Talha, also reported from al-Kisa'i, read actively: the called soul does not carry anything, with شيئا as object.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r4.anchor: وأبو السمال وطلحة - وتروى عن الكسائي - بفتح التاء من فوق وكسر الميم. أسند الفعل إلى ضمير النفس المحذوفة

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r5.claim: ذا قربى may describe the person asked to carry the burden or the caller; both senses are good.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r5.anchor: ولو كان ذا قربى } [أي:] ولو كان المدعو ذا قربى. وقيل: التقدير: ولو كان الداعي ذا قربى. والمعنيان حسنان.

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r6.claim: A nominative ذو reading treats كان as complete, meaning if a relative were present, as in the cited example and 2:280.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r6.anchor: وقرئ " ذو " بالرفع، على أنها التامة أي: ولو حضر/ ذو قربى نحو: " قد كان من مطر " ، وإن كان ذو عسرة

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari prefers incomplete كان because the wording fits the person summoned being a relative; treating it as complete disrupts the connection.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ونظم الكلام أحسن ملاءمة للناقصة؛ لأن المعنى: على أن المثقلة إذا دعت أحدا إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء، ولو كان مدعوها ذا قربى

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r8.claim: بالغيب can be circumstantial of the subject, fearing God while unseen from Him, or of the object, God unseen from them.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r8.anchor: قوله: بالغيب " حال من الفاعل أي: يخشونه غائبين عنه، أو من المفعول أي: غائبا عنهم.

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r9.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r9.claim: The common forms تزكى and يتزكى retain تاء of the tafa'ul pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r9.anchor: قوله: " ومن تزكى " قرأ العامة " تزكى " تفعل، " فإنما يتزكى " يتفعل.

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r10.claim: Abu Amr reads يزكى in both places, assimilating original تاء into زاي, as يتذكر becomes يذكرون.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r10.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو " ومن يزكى " " فإنما يزكى " والأصل فيهما: يتزكى فأدغمت التاء في الزاي

SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وطلحة
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r11.claim: Ibn Masud and Talha read ازكى, using hamzat al-wasl for assimilation; the second form assimilates like Abu Amr's variant.
SAMIN-DURR:35:18/r11.anchor: وابن مسعود وطلحة " ومن ازكى " والأصل: تزكى فأدغم باجتلاب همزة الوصل

ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n15/r1.claim: The statement concerns Judgment Day and echoes 6:164, which also says each person's wrongdoing rests on that person alone.
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n15/r1.anchor: I.e., on Judgment Day - for "whatever [wrongj any human being commits rests upon him alone" (6:164

ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r1.claim: Asad reads the first clause as denying the Christian doctrine of original sin burdening humanity.
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r1.anchor: the first part of the above statement implies a negation of the Christian doctrine of "original sin" with which mankind is supposedly burdened

ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r2.claim: Asad reads the second clause as categorically refuting the doctrine that Jesus vicariously atones for that sin.
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r2.anchor: the second part categorically refutes the doctrine of the "vicarious atonement" of that sin by Jesus.

ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r3.claim: Asad directs readers to 53:38 and the corresponding note as a parallel statement.
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n16/r3.anchor: See also 53 :38 and the corresponding note 31.

ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n17/r1.claim: Only those who believe in realities beyond human perception can benefit from the warning; Asad points to 2:3, 27:80–81, and 30:52–53.
ASAD-NOTES:35:18#n17/r1.anchor: only those "who believe in the existence of that which is beyond the reach of human perception" can really benefit

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r8.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ says the pronoun in the parallel phrase is taken by some to refer to God, but prefers the Day of Judgment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r8.anchor: والضمير في {مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ} الله - عز وجل - عند من تأولوه بذلك، وليوم القيامة على التأويل الأرجح

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r9.claim: Attributing the splitting to the sky and earth is figurative, presenting their spontaneous compliance as if no agent were needed.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r9.anchor: وإسناد النفطار والتفطر إلى السماء والأرض، هو من الإسناد المجازي الدال على طواعية تلقائية كأنه يستغنى بها عن فاعل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r10.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r10.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r10.claim: The root appears in Qur'anic usage only with a divine sense: God creates the heavens and earth, and fiṭra is humanity's original nature from God.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r10.anchor: وفي القرآن الكريم، لا يأتي (فطر، وفاطر) إلا بدلالة إسلامية، لله - عز وجل - فاطر السموات والأرض، والفطرة الخلقة الأصلية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r11.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r11.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r11.claim: Arabic uses the root for cracking teeth, grape tips, and feet; breakfast usage extends from the break in nighttime hunger, and fuṭūr means a fissure.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p506/r11.anchor: ومن استعمال المادة في العربية: فطر الناب، ورءوس العنب عن تشقق، ومنه: تفطرت قدماه إذا تشققت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r1.claim: Warning is not restricted to unbelievers and hypocrites: believers are warned as a reminder to fulfill their duties, and the Qur’an also addresses the Prophet’s kin and those fearing resurrection.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r1.anchor: الإنذار في القرآن الكريم لا يكون خاصاً للكفار والمنافقين وقد يأتي الإنذار للمؤمنين والكافرين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r1.claim: No sinful soul bears the sin of another; each soul bears its own burden.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r2.claim: This does not conflict with 29:13: misleaders carry their own sins plus sins caused by misleading others, not the actual sins of those followers; the added burden is their own incitement and causation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r2.anchor: ولا منافاة بين هذا وقوله تعالى في سورة العنكبوت

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r3.claim: A مثقلة is a soul weighed down by sins; it calls someone to take or lighten its burden, the sin that oppresses it.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r4.claim: An alternative construes إلى حملها as a call to bear the burden of its load.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r5.claim: No one responds by carrying any part of the soul’s burden; the initial negation concerns voluntary, generous assistance and rebuts sinners’ claim that others would carry their sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r5.anchor: نفي للحمل الإختياري تكرما من نفس الحامل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r6.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r6.claim: The reported occasion is that al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra told believers to reject Muḥammad and promised to carry their sins; the verse was revealed in response.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#4/r6.anchor: أن الوليد بن المغيرة قال لقوم من المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r1.claim: The second clause denies carrying even after the burdened soul asks, thus covering voluntary and forced carrying, every kind of burden and any possible carrier; if none is compelled after a request, none is compelled without one.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r1.anchor: وهذا نفي للحمل بعد الطلب من الوازرة أعم من أن يكون إختيارا أو جبرا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r2.claim: One distinction is that the first clause denies transferring the entire burden, while the second denies even lessening it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r2.anchor: إن في الأولى نفي حمل جميع الوزر بحيث يتعرى منه المحمول عنه وفي الثاني نفي التخفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r3.claim: Another distinction says the first clause denies forced carrying and the second voluntary carrying; the objection is that the wording should then reverse these cases and explicitly name coercion.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r3.anchor: إن الأول نفي الحمل إجبارا والثاني نفي له إختيارا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r4.claim: A further distinction assigns complete justice to the first clause and the absence of any refuge from that day’s terror to the second; al-Ālūsī prefers his broader reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r4.anchor: الجملة الأولى كما دلت على أن المثقل بالذنوب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r5.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r5.claim: An objection asks why the wording specifies a sinful soul instead of saying that no soul bears another’s burden, which would state the generality more explicitly and concisely.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r5.anchor: عدم حمل الغير على الغير عام في النفس الآثمة وغير الآثمة فلم خص بالآثمة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r6.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r6.claim: The reply is that the discussion concerns sinners punished for their own sins, not for deeds committed by someone else.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r6.anchor: وجوابه أن الكلام في أرباب الأوزار المعذبين لبيان أن عذابهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r7.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r7.claim: A second objection asks how وزر can follow تزر without redundancy, since lexicons define وزر as bearing a heavy thing or sin; the proposed answer calls it grammatical tajrīd.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r7.anchor: أن معنى وزر حمل الوزر لا مطلق الحمل على ما في النهاية الأثيرية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r8.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r8.claim: A third objection asks what benefit وازرة adds if the active participle is already implied by تزر; the response is that it presents the soul as already characterized by bearing, and an indefinite participle under negation also generalizes.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r8.anchor: أن ( وازرة ) يفهم من تزر كما يفهم ضارب من يضرب

ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r9.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r9.claim: The scholar’s answer is that an active participle marks an established quality concurrent with the action; its indefinite use under negation adds generality, contrary to al-Taftāzānī’s claim that the participle adds little.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p184#5/r9.anchor: وهذه فائدة جليلة ويزيدها جلالة إستفادة العموم إذا أورد أسم الفاعل نكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the wording needs no grammatical tajrīd: lexicons define وزر يزر as bearing a burden.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r1.anchor: وفي القاموس وزره كوعده وزرا بالكسر حمله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r2.claim: Together the clauses state the general rule raised in the first objection while preserving added benefit in their separate phrasing.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r2.anchor: وأنت تعلم أنه من مجموع الجملتين يستفاد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r3.speaker: أبو السمال عن طلحة وإبراهيم عن الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r3.claim: They read لا تحمل with second-person feminine tāʾ and a kasra on mīm; شيء is accusative, and the subject is the person called: if a burdened soul asks someone to carry, that person carries none of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r3.anchor: عن الكسائي ( لا تحمل ) بفتح التاء المثناة من فوق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r4.claim: The implied subject of كان is the person summoned, even if that person is related to the caller; this is more natural than making the caller the subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r4.anchor: والأول أحسن لأن الداعي هو المثقلة بعينه

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya instead makes the subject of كان the caller, so the phrase means even if the caller is related to the person called.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r5.anchor: إبن عطية : اسم كان ضمير الداعي

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the masculine pronoun follows the meaning of مثقلة, which denotes any person, not only a grammatically feminine individual; al-Ālūsī says the point is evident.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r6.anchor: وقول أبي حيان ذكر الضمير حملا على المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r7.claim: This is a fresh statement identifying those who heed the warnings: only those who fear their Lord benefit, unlike the rebellious and obstinate.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r7.anchor: إستئناف مسوق لبيان من يتعظ بما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r8.claim: بالغيب can mean fearing God while unseen from His punishment, while alone away from people, or fearing punishment that is itself unseen; the phrase is circumstantial of the subject or object.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r8.anchor: أي يخشونه تعالى غائبين عن عذابه سبحانه أو عن الناس في خلواتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r9.claim: Establishing prayer means observing it properly and making it a raised beacon and standard.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r9.anchor: وأقاموا الصلاة أي راعوها كما ينبغي وجعلوها منارا منصوبا وعلما مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r10.claim: The difference in verbal forms is explained by the earlier discussion of 35:9, “God sends the winds, then they stir a cloud.”
ALUSI-FULL:v22p185/r10.anchor: في قوله تعالى ( الله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r1.claim: تزكى means purifying oneself from sins and their stains by being affected by these warnings.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r1.anchor: تطهر من أدناس الأوزار والمعاصي بالتأثر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r2.claim: Purification benefits only the person who undertakes it, just as sin’s defilement harms only its agent; purification includes fearing God and establishing prayer, so the verse reinforces and urges both.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r2.anchor: لإقتصار نفعه عليها كما أن من تدنس بها لا يتدنس إلا عليها والتزكي شامل للخشية

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r3.speaker: العباس عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r3.claim: He reads ومن يزكى فإنما يزكي with yāʾ and a doubled zāy in both verbs, from يتزكى by assimilation of tāʾ into zāy, as in يذكرون.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r3.anchor: عن أبي عمرو ( ومن يزكى فإنما يزكي )

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وطلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ṭalḥa read ومن أزكى, assimilating tāʾ into zāy and adding a connecting hamza at the start; Ṭalḥa also reads فإنما تزكى with assimilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r4.anchor: إبن مسعود وطلحة ( ومن أزكى ) بإدغام التاء

ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r5.claim: The return is to God alone, with no other independently or jointly, and He rewards those who purify themselves with the best recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p186/r5.anchor: لا إلى أحد غيره إستقلالا أو إشتراكا فيجازيهم على تزكيهم أحسن الجزاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r1.claim: Those who fear their Lord unseen fear Him without having seen Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r1.anchor: {إنما تنذر الذين يخشون} يخافون، {ربهم بالغيب} ولم يروه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash says the Prophet's warning benefits only those who fear their Lord unseen.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r2.anchor: وقال الأخفش: تأويله أي: إنذارك إنما ينفع الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r3.claim: Purifying oneself means becoming righteous and doing good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r3.anchor: صلح وعمل خيرا، {فإنما يتزكى لنفسه} لها ثوابه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r4.claim: The one who purifies himself receives its reward for himself.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#2/r5.claim: The final return is to God.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r1.claim: After establishing truth with decisive proofs and threatening seizure, Biqāʿī argues that punishment presupposes sin; everyone has some burden that warrants it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r1.anchor: وكان العقاب لا يكون حكمه إلا عند الذنب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r2.claim: No one is punished at resurrection or during seizure by carrying another’s sin; each is liable only for what that person committed.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r2.anchor: لا تحمل حاملة من جهة الإثم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r3.claim: The verse says a sin-bearing soul, rather than simply a soul, because no soul fit to bear a burden is free of a burden of its own; only God protects from sin.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r3.anchor: ولما لم تكن نفس متأهلة للحمل تخلو من وزر تحمله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r4.claim: Each person has deeds, directly or causally, that establish the case against that person; no one is seized for another’s personal sin, unlike worldly tyrants.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r4.anchor: لا تؤخذ نفس بذنب أخرى الذي يخصها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r5.claim: Even a soul weighed down by disbelief or other sins cannot get another person to carry any part of its uniquely personal burden to lessen its punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r5.anchor: أي بالذنوب سواء كانت كفرا أو غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r6.claim: No one carries any portion of the burden, willingly or by compulsion.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r7.claim: Kinship gives no exemption, whether the relative is the one calling for help or the one asked to carry the burden.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r8.claim: The first statement says no one is destroyed for another’s sin; the second says no one’s own sin is removed for another to save them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r8.anchor: أنه لا يهلك أحد بذنب غيره بل بذنب نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r9.claim: Although the rule is clear, it is heart-rending; one wonders at anyone who hears it without fear. Only those who benefit from turning back are effectively its audience.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p214/r9.anchor: أي إنذارا يفيد الرجوع عن الغي , فلاختصاصهم بالنفع كانوا كأنهم مختصون بالإنذار

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r1.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r1.claim: Al-Qushayrī defines warning as informing someone of the place of danger.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r2.claim: The imperfect form depicts fear practiced now and maintained into the future.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r2.anchor: أي يوقعون هذا الفعل في الحال يواظبون عليه في الاستقبال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r3.claim: The wisest fear their benefactor, since even a small punishment could end His beneficence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r3.anchor: أعقل الناس من خاف المحسن لأن أقل عقابه قطع إحسانه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r4.claim: The phrase may mean that they fear what remains unseen, or that they fear God while unseen by anyone who might otherwise witness their devotion.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r5.claim: The highest believers remain sincere in private and public, trusting the messenger’s report of unseen matters without needing a miracle or unveiling.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r6.claim: Biqāʿī says he knows no one who matched Khadīja and al-Ṣiddīq in this sincere faith in the unseen.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r6.anchor: ولا نعلم أحدا وازى خديجة والصديق رضي الله عنهما في ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r7.claim: Prayer gathers inward and outward submission and is the noblest worship.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r8.claim: Establishing prayer means guarding all its limits at all times, a strong sign of sincerity; its past tense suits the fixed prayer times, five prayers and their associated sunnas.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r8.anchor: وكانت إقامتها بمعنى حفظ جميع حدودها في كل حال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r9.claim: Tazakkā means to purify oneself and increase in these virtues; its form suggests the great effort needed to overcome the soul’s pull toward defilement.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r10.claim: Biqāʿī supplies an implied contrast: the corrupt person’s defilement harms only that person, just as the purified person’s growth benefits that person.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r10.anchor: ومن تدسى فإنما يتدسى على نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r11.claim: Purification benefits the person who undertakes it; emphasis is needed because people may overlook that the benefit is specifically their own.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r11.anchor: قد يغفل عن أن هذا نفع له وخاص به

BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r12.claim: All return to God, who fully discloses His attributes in the resurrection and recompenses each person’s deeds, vindicating the Prophet against those who accept or reject his warning.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p215/r12.anchor: الذي يكشف عن جميع صفاته أتم كشف تحتمله العقول يوم البعث لا إلى غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.claim: God’s selective granting of receptive hearing explains why warning benefits those He wills, confirming the earlier statement that only those who fear God gain from it and consoling the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r12.anchor: وإن الإنذار إنما هو لمن قضى بانتفاعه

DURR-FULL:v7p16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r1.speaker: أبو رمثة
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r1.claim: Abu Rimtha reports the Prophet asking his father whether he was his son, then saying neither incurs the other’s guilt and reciting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r1.anchor: عن أبي رمثة قال: انطلقت مع أبي نحو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما رأيته قال لأبي: ابنك هذا قال: أي ورب الكعبة

DURR-FULL:v7p16/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r2.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r2.claim: Ata al-Khurasani says a soul burdened with sins may call a relative or stranger, but none can carry any of its sins for it.
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r2.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني في قوله {وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها} قال: إن تدع نفس مثقلة من الخطايا ذا قرابة أو غير ذي قرابة

DURR-FULL:v7p16/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person bearing sin will find no one who can carry any of that burden away.
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء} يكون عليه وزر لا يجد أحدا يحمل عنه من وزره شيئا

DURR-FULL:v7p16/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r4.claim: Mujahid says the image of the burdened soul calling for help conveys the same rule as ‘no bearer bears another’s burden.’
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء} كنحو {ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

DURR-FULL:v7p16/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r5.claim: Ikrima reports that on Judgment Day a neighbor, a disbeliever, a parent, or a spouse may plead for help; even a believer interceding for a disbeliever can only reduce his rank in Hell, while family members refuse to surrender a good deed because they fear for themselves.
DURR-FULL:v7p16/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: إن الجار يتعلق بجاره يوم القيامة فيقول: يا رب سل هذا لم كان يغلق بابه دوني

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r1.claim: The verse's rule is echoed by the day when a parent cannot avail a child and when a person flees close kin.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r1.anchor: ويقول الله (يوم لا يجزي والد عن ولده) (لقمان 133)

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r2.claim: The burden that the weighed-down person calls others to help carry means her sins; no close relative bears any of them.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها} أي إلى ذنوبها {لا يحمل منه شيء

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r3.claim: Fearing their Lord unseen means fearing the Fire and the reckoning.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r3.anchor: {إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب} أي يخشون النار والحساب

DURR-FULL:v7p17/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r4.claim: Purification for oneself means that whoever performs a righteous deed acts for his own benefit.
DURR-FULL:v7p17/r4.anchor: وفي قوله {ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه} أي من عمل عملا صالحا فإنما يعمل لنفسه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r1.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r1.claim: A heavy soul burdened by sins may call on a relative or anyone else, but nobody can carry away any of its sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r1.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني في قوله : وان تدع مثقلة إلى حملها قال : ان تدع نفس مثقلة من الخطايا ذا قرابة أو غير ذي قرابة لا يحمل ، عنها من خطاياها شيء

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says that a person bearing a burden will find no one to carry away any of it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما في قوله : وان تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء يكون عليه وزر لا يجد احدا يحمل ، عنه من وزره شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r3.claim: Mujahid treats the statement about a burdened soul as equivalent to the rule that no bearer bears another’s burden.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : وان تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منها شيء كنحو ولا تزر وازرة وزر اخرى

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r4.claim: Ikrima describes neighbors, believers and unbelievers, and parents and children pleading with one another at resurrection; even intercession only lowers the unbeliever’s station within the Fire, while a child fears giving a parent even a small portion of merit. He links this to two verses about kin abandoning kin.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : ان الجار يتعلق بجاره يوم القيامة فيقول : يا رب سل هذا لم كان يغلق بابي دوني

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r5.claim: Qatada says the burden is sin, even a close relative cannot take it on, those fearing God unseen fear the Fire and reckoning, and purification benefits its doer; he contrasts living believers with unbelievers dead in trace, sight, heart, intention, and deed.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3177#3/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : وان تدع مثقلة إلى حملها اي إلى ذنوبها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى قال : قرابة قريبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr’s preferred reading is reassurance that Muslims will not be collectively annihilated, like the deliverance in Yūsuf 12:110 and the forgiveness in al-Anfāl 8:33; this reading is broader and better.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r1.anchor: ولهذا فالظاهر أن هذا تأمين للمسلمين من الاستئصال كقوله تعالى : { وما كان الله معذبهم وهم يستغفرون } ( الأنفال : 33 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r2.claim: An alternative takes the rule as applying at resurrection: God may remove everyone without punishing believers in the hereafter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد : ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى يوم القيامة ، أي إن يشأ يذهبكم جميعا ولا يعذب المؤمنين في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r3.claim: The Prophet said that people will be resurrected according to their intentions, cited for the alternative afterlife interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r3.anchor: وهذا كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ثم يحشرون على نياتهم ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r4.claim: The universal rule is compatible with al-ʿAnkabūt 29:12: a person does not bear another’s sin when they had no part in committing it, while misguiding leaders do share responsibility for those they enticed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r4.anchor: الجمع بين الآيتين أن هذه الآية نفت أن يحمل أحد وزر آخر لا مشاركة له للحامل على اقتراف الوزر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r5.claim: Wizr originally means a burden, like wiqr in both weight and sense; wazara means to carry, so the verse says no bearer carries another’s load.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r5.anchor: وأصل الوزر بكسر الواو : هو الوقر بوزنه ومعناه . وهو الحمل بكسر الحاء ، أي ما يحمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r6.claim: Wāzira is feminine because it means a soul; the wording states that God does not assign one soul another’s load as an act of justice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r6.anchor: وجرى وصف الوازرة على التأنيث لأنه أريد به النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r7.claim: The feminine form foregrounds nafs rather than masculine person because ‘soul’ naturally comes to mind with earning, as in al-Anʿām and al-Muddaththir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p287/r7.anchor: ووجه اختيار الإسناد إلى المؤنث بتأويل النفس دون أن يجري الإضمار على التذكير بتأويل الشخص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r1.claim: The rule extends to a burdened soul begging someone to carry all or part of its sins: no one will help, lest people project earthly customs onto the hereafter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r1.anchor: ثم نبه على أن هذا الحكم العادل مطرد مستمر حتى لو استغاثت نفس مثقلة بالأوزار من ينتدب لحمل أوزارها أو بعضها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r2.claim: Calling the appeal duʿāʾ evokes a plea for rescue: Arabs conventionally answered calls for aid even when helping harmed them, as the proverb about the generous man called to his death says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r2.anchor: ولذلك سمي طلب الحمل هنا دعاء لأن في الدعاء معنى الاستغاثة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r3.speaker: وداك بن ثميل المازني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r3.claim: Waddāk ibn Thumayl al-Māzinī’s verse says that when people seek aid, the noble do not ask which battle or place, illustrating the Arab ideal of answering a plea.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r3.anchor: وقال وداك بن ثميل المازني : إذا استنجدوا لم يسألوا من دعاهم لأية حرب أم بأي مكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r4.claim: The object of tadʿu is omitted to make it general: the burdened soul may call on anyone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r4.anchor: وحذف مفعول تدع } لقصد العموم . والتقدير : وإن تدع مثقلة أي مدعو .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r5.claim: The call is directed ‘to carrying’ because carrying is its cause and aim; an implied request to someone to bear the load is omitted but understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r5.anchor: وجعل الدعاء إلى الحمل لأن الحمل سبب الدعاء وعلته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r6.claim: The scene concerns the hereafter: even a soul crying out for someone to remove part of its sins, including an alleged idol intercessor, finds no responder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p288/r6.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى ما سيكون في الآخرة ، أي لو استصرخت نفس من يحمل عنها شيئا من أوزارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r1.claim: The concessive لو clause is circumstantial to the burdened soul; the hidden subject of kāna is the omitted person she called, and conditional indefiniteness becomes distributive in the positive clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r1.anchor: المحذوف ، إذ تقديره : وإن تدع مثقلة أحدا إلى حملها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r2.claim: The concessive intensifies the claim because kin are especially tender and might be imagined to share the burden and reduce punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r2.anchor: ووجه ما اقتضته المبالغة من { لو } الوصلية أن ذا القربى أرق وأشفق على قريبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r3.claim: Kinship here is unrestricted and includes close relations such as parents and spouses, who will flee from each other on that day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r3.anchor: والإطلاق في القربى يشمل قريب القرابة كالأبوين والزوجين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r4.claim: The verse rejects any self-sufficient rescue through family solidarity: polytheists imagined patrons and intercessors, but no one bears another’s sin at the gathering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r4.anchor: وهذا إبطال لاعتقاد الغناء الذاتي بالتضامن والتحامل فقد كان المشركون يقيسون أمور الآخرة على أمور الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r5.claim: This does not deny intercession granted by God’s permission to honor Muḥammad, or divinely granted expiation such as believing children interceding for their bereaved believing mothers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r5.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي الشفاعة الواردة في الحديث ، كما تقدم في سورة سبأ ، فإنها إنما تكون بإذن الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r6.claim: The next clause answers the Messenger’s inward wonder that most polytheists remain unmoved: warning benefits believers and those prepared to believe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r6.anchor: استئناف بياني لأن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطر في نفسه التعجب من عدم تأثر أكثر المشركين بإنذاره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r7.claim: This continuation confirms that the prior verse primarily admonishes polytheists about resurrection and judgment, and indirectly assures Muslims against a general punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p289/r7.anchor: وإيراد هذه الآية عقب التي قبلها يؤكد أن المقصد الأول من التي قبلها موعظة المشركين وتخويفهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r1.claim: ‘Warning’ means achieving its effect—abstention or belief—not merely delivering a threat, since the Prophet repeatedly warned the polytheists already.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r1.anchor: وأطلق الإنذار هنا على حصول أثره ، وهو الانكفاف أو التصديق به ، وليس المراد حقيقة الإنذار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r2.claim: The restriction is qasr qalb, correcting the assumption that unbelievers benefit from warning; although literal exclusivity is possible, context makes it relative, as in Yāsīn and Qāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r2.anchor: فالمقصود من القصر أنه قصر قلب لأن المقصود التنبيه على أن لا يظن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انتفاع الذين لا يؤمنون بنذارته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r3.claim: Al-ghayb is what is absent from sight: these people fear God privately, unseen by others, with sincere rather than performative faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r3.anchor: والغيب : ما غاب عنك ، أي الذين يخشون ربهم في خلواتهم وعند غيبتهم عن العيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r4.claim: Establishing prayer implies that they have not neglected any prayer, as the idiom of establishing prayer already indicates in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r4.anchor: أي لم يفرطوا في صلاة كما يؤذن به فعل الإقامة كما تقدم في أول سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r5.claim: These two traits identify Muslims; naming them by descriptive clauses rather than their familiar title both expands the wording and praises sincerity in belief and practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r5.anchor: فعدل عن استحضارهم بأشهر ألقابهم مع ما فيه من الإيجاز إلى استحضارهم بصلتين مع ما فيهما من الإطناب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r6.claim: The purification clause is a proverbial tadhyīl; placing the general maxim after the preceding statement shows that those warned believers are already included in it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p290/r6.anchor: وجملة { ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه } تذييل جار مجرى المثل .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r1.claim: The restriction means accepting the warning benefits the hearers themselves; those who disregard it abandon self-purification and harm only themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r1.anchor: والمقصود من القصر في قوله : { فإنما يتزكى لنفسه } أن قبولهم النذارة كان لفائدة أنفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r2.claim: The final clause completes the maxim: everyone, purified or not, returns to God and receives fitting recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r2.anchor: والتعريف في { المصير } للجنس ، أي المصير كله إلى الله سواء فيه مصير المتزكي ومصير غير المتزكي ، أي وكل يجازى بما يناسبه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r3.claim: Fronting ‘to God’ draws attention to a destination whose divine attributes ensure justice and generosity, while also serving the verse’s cadence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p291/r3.anchor: وتقديم المجرور في قوله : { وإلى الله المصير } للاهتمام للتنبيه على أنه مصير إلى من اقتضى اسمه الجليل الصفات المناسبة لإقامة العدل

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r1.claim: A responsible person should worship and fear God rather than defy Him, and should not be worse than inanimate things despite being creation's noblest kind.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r1.anchor: فينبغي للعاقل المكلف أن يعبد الله ويخافه ولا يجترىء على ما يخالف رضاه

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r2.speaker: جعفر الطيار
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r2.claim: Ja'far al-Tayyar recounts that the Prophet asked a mountain to greet him and provide water; the mountain replied that fear of 2:24 had made it weep until its water was gone.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r2.anchor: قال جعفر الطيار رضي الله عنه : كنت مع النبي عليه السلام وكان حذاءنا جبل

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r3.claim: The author gives two verb forms: wazara-yaziru, with the verbal noun wazr, and wazara-yūzaru, meaning to carry.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r3.anchor: يقال وزر يزر من الثاني وزرا بالفتح والكسر ووزر يوزر من الرابع حمل

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r4.claim: Wizr means sin and burden; wāzira and ukhrā describe an omitted feminine soul, so the sense is that no sinful soul bears another's guilt at resurrection.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r4.anchor: والوزر الإثم والثقل والوازرة صفة للنفس المحذوفة وكذا أخرى

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r5.claim: Each soul bears the sins it acquired; in worldly life, by contrast, tyrants may punish one ally or neighbor for another.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r5.anchor: لا تحمل نفس آثمة يوم القيامة إثم نفس أخرى بحيث تتعرى منه المحمول عنها

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r6.claim: The extra loads in 29:13 are the deceivers' own sins of misguidance and leading others astray, not the victims' sins; 29:12's promise to bear others' errors is expressly denied.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r6.anchor: فهو حمل أثقال ضلالهم مع أثقال إضلالهم وكلاهما أوزارهم ليس فيها شيء من أوزار غيرهم

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r7.claim: When oppressors are charged with victims' sins, the charge is actually recompense for their transgressive oppression, though it appears to lighten the victim's load.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r7.anchor: فإن المحمول في الحقيقة جزاء الظلم وإن كان يحصل في الظاهر تخفيف حمل المظلوم

BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r8.claim: Each creature has a particular secret and relation with God and is accountable for its own endowment, just as each seed grows only the plant stored within it; Bursevī cites al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya.
BURSEVI:v7p261#3/r8.anchor: أن الله تعالى في خلق كل واحد من الخلق سرا مخصوصا به وله مع كل واحد شأن آخر

BURSEVI:v7p262/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r1.speaker: سعدي
BURSEVI:v7p262/r1.claim: Saadi's couplet reinforces the image that each seed bears only its own kind of fruit.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r1.anchor: رطب ناورد وب خر زهره بار ه تخم افيكنى بر همان شم دار

BURSEVI:v7p262/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r2.claim: The verb is feminine singular and means if she calls, with the soul understood as its subject.

BURSEVI:v7p262/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r3.claim: The burdened one is a soul weighed down by sins; the object of her appeal is omitted and understood as another person.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r3.anchor: أي : نفس أثقلتها الأوزار والمفعول محذوف أي : أحدا

BURSEVI:v7p262/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v7p262/r4.claim: Al-Raghib says heaviness and lightness are opposites: the term began with physical weight and extends metaphorically to debts and sins.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : الثقل والخفة متقابلان وكل ما يترجح عما يوزن به

BURSEVI:v7p262/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r5.claim: Sin is called a weight because it burdens its bearer on judgment day and holds the sinner back from reward in this life.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r5.anchor: فالثقل الإثم سمي به لأنه يثقل صاحبه يوم القيامة ويثبطه عن الثواب في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v7p262/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r6.claim: The appeal is for someone to carry some of the sins already resting on the burdened soul.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r6.anchor: الذي عليها من الذنوب ليحمل بعضها

BURSEVI:v7p262/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r7.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v7p262/r7.claim: Al-Mufradat distinguishes ḥiml, with kasra, for an external load from ḥaml, with fatha, for an internal burden such as a child in the womb.

BURSEVI:v7p262/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r8.claim: The person asked does not agree to carry any part of the sins.

BURSEVI:v7p262/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r9.claim: Wa-law is connective here; kāna refers to the omitted person addressed in the appeal, making the statement cover every possible helper.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r9.anchor: {ولو} للوصل {كان} أي : المدعو المفهوم من الدعوة وترك ذكره ليشمل كل مدعو

BURSEVI:v7p262/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r10.claim: Even a close relative of the caller, such as a parent, child, or sibling, cannot help, since each person is overwhelmed by their own concern and load.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r10.anchor: ذا قرابة من الداعي كالأب والأم والولد والأخ ونحو ذلك

BURSEVI:v7p262/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r11.claim: The verse shows that God holds only the sinner accountable and that appealing to relatives cannot avail those who lack piety.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r11.anchor: ففي هذا دليل أنه تعالى لا يؤاخذ بالذنب إلا جانيه وأن الاستغاثة بالأقربين غير نافعة لغير المتقين

BURSEVI:v7p262/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v7p262/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that on judgment day parents ask their child to carry some sins, but the child refuses; a husband similarly asks his wife for even a speck of good, and she says she fears for herself.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يلقى الأب والأم ابنه فيقول يا بني احمل عني بعض ذنوبي

BURSEVI:v7p262/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r13.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet says kinship and friendship cannot save a person from the reckoning when everyone is preoccupied with their own fate.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r13.anchor: هي رحمى نه برادر به برادر دارد

BURSEVI:v7p262/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r14.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v7p262/r14.claim: Al-Irshad distinguishes the clauses: the current one denies voluntary burden-bearing, while the preceding clause denies being made to bear another's sin by force.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r14.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : هذه الآية نفي للتحمل اختيارا والأولى نفي له إجبارا

BURSEVI:v7p262/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p262/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p262/r15.claim: Obedience is light and disobedience darkness; neither quality transfers between people, and at the crossing each walks by their own light without another's light passing to them.
BURSEVI:v7p262/r15.anchor: أن الطاعة نور والعصيان ظلمة فإذا اتصف جوهر الإنسان بصفة النور أو بصفة الظلمة

BURSEVI:v7p263/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r1.claim: Warning is communicating a message together with causing fear.

BURSEVI:v7p263/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r2.claim: The addressees are those who fear their Lord while unseen, either because punishment and the afterlife's rulings are unseen to them or because they fear privately, away from people.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r2.anchor: غائبين عن عذابه وأحكام الآخرة أو عن الناس في خلواتهم

BURSEVI:v7p263/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r3.claim: On the first reading, the phrase is circumstantial of the object; on the private-devotion reading, it is circumstantial of the subject who fears.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r3.anchor: فهو حال من الفاعل أو حال كون ذلك العذاب غائبا عنهم فهو حال من المفعول

BURSEVI:v7p263/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r4.claim: They observe prayer as it should be observed, making it a raised beacon and an upright standard.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r4.anchor: راعوها كما ينبغي وجعلوها منارا منصوبا وعلما مرفوعا

BURSEVI:v7p263/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r5.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p263/r5.claim: Kashf al-Asrar explains the varied wording by noting that fear is continuous, whereas prayer times are fixed and pass.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r5.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" وغاير بين اللفظين لأن أوقات الخشية دائمة وأوقات الصلاة معينة منقضية

BURSEVI:v7p263/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r6.claim: The warning benefits these people, though the Prophet warns everyone; fear and prayer are singled out as roots of inward and outward good deeds, prayer being religion's pillar and fear a sign of certainty.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r6.anchor: والمعنى إنما ينفع إنذارك وتحذيرك هؤلاء من قومك دون من عداهم من أهل التمرد والفساد

BURSEVI:v7p263/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r7.claim: Fear of God rises with knowledge of Him, as 35:28 says; a heart without knowledge and fear is dead and unmoved by warning, as 36:70 describes the living recipient.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r7.anchor: كما قال تعالى : {ومن الناس والدوآب والانعام مختلف ألوانه}

BURSEVI:v7p263/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p263/r8.claim: A hadith says that abandoning prayer stands between a person and polytheism and unbelief.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن بين الرجل وبين الشرك والكفر ترك الصلاة"

BURSEVI:v7p263/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r9.claim: The person purified has shed sins and disobedience by responding to these warnings and has repaired their state through acts of obedience.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r9.anchor: تطهر من أوضار الأوزار والمعاصي بالتأثر من هذه الإنذارات وأصلح حاله بفعل الطاعات

BURSEVI:v7p263/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r10.claim: Purification benefits only its practitioner, just as sin's stain harms only its bearer; one who gives alms also earns its reward for oneself.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r10.anchor: لاقتصار نفعه عليها كما أن من تدنس بها لا يتدنس إلا عليها

BURSEVI:v7p263/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r11.claim: All return is to God alone, who rewards purification; purification from sin earns Paradise and its degrees, while release from attachment to all besides God earns His beauty.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r11.anchor: واعلم أن ثواب التزكي عن المعاصي هو الجنة ودرجاتها

BURSEVI:v7p263/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p263/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p263/r12.claim: One who freely returns to God finds no lasting repose in anything below Him.
BURSEVI:v7p263/r12.anchor: فمن رجع إلى الله بالاختيار لم يبق له بما دونه قرار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī says the preceding material has already been explained in Sūrat Ibrāhīm and al-Anʿām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r1.anchor: وما بعد هذا قد تقدم بيانه إبراهيم الأنعام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r2.claim: A burdened soul is weighed down by sins; its load is the sins it has incurred.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ إلى حملها ﴾ الذي حملت من الخطايا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r3.claim: No one can carry any part of another soul’s burden, even if the one asked is a close relative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ﴾ الذي تدعوه ﴿ ذا قربى ﴾ ذا قرابة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r4.claim: Those who fear their Lord unseen do so without having seen Him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r5.claim: The warning benefits those who fear God; it is as though they alone are warned because they alone benefit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r5.anchor: والمعنى إنما تنفع بانذارك أهل الخشية فكأنك تنذرهم دون غيرهم لمكان اختصاصهم بالانتفاع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r6.claim: Purification here is cleansing oneself of idolatry and indecencies while doing good.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r6.anchor: أي تطهر من الشرك والفواحش وفعل الخير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r7.claim: The benefit of purification belongs to the person who purifies himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r7.anchor: فانما يتزكى لنفسه أي فصلاحه لنفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p482#2/r8.claim: All return to God, who will recompense them for their deeds.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r1.claim: Only people of insight and understanding who fear their Lord unseen and do what He commands take heed of the Prophet's message.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r1.anchor: أي: إنما يتعظ بما جئت به أولو البصائر والنهى، الخائفون من ربهم، الفاعلون ما أمرهم به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r2.claim: Whoever purifies himself by doing good works brings the benefit back to himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r2.anchor: أي: ومن عمل صالحا فإنما يعود نفعه على نفسه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r3.claim: Everyone returns to God, who reckons swiftly and rewards each person according to their deeds, good for good and evil for evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p542/r3.anchor: أي: وإليه المرجع والمآب، وهو سريع الحساب، وسيجزي كل عامل بعمله، إن خيرا فخير، وإن شرا فشر

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r2.claim: The verb is grammatically indicative because the sense is “no bearer bears”; its declarative form carries the force of a prohibition.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r2.anchor: (ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى) رفع؛ لأن المعنى ليست تزر، فهذا خبر في اللفظ، نهي في المعنى

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r3.claim: “Even if he were a near relative” refers to the person just mentioned.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r3.anchor: (ولو كان ذا قربى) أي: لو كان المذكور ذا قربى

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r7.claim: No person is held accountable for another person’s sin.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r7.anchor: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى أي: لا تحمل حاملة حمل أخرى، يعني: لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب أحد

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r8.claim: If a soul weighed down by sins asks another to bear some of its burden, none will carry any of it, even the closest relative.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r8.anchor: وإن تدع مثقلة أي: حاملة حملا ثقيلا إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى أي: ذا قرابة

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r9.claim: The verse singles out the burdened woman because women are weaker, evoke more compassion, and are likelier to receive help; if even she is not relieved, others are even less likely to be.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r9.anchor: وإنما خص المثقلة؛ لأنهن أضعف، والقلوب لهن أرق، والناس إلى معونتهن أميل

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r10.claim: No one carries another’s sin because of the gravity of sins and fear of punishment; each person is taken for their own sin.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r10.anchor: وإنما لا يحمل لوجهين: إحدهما: غلظ حال الآثام، وثانيهما: ما فيه من مخافة العذاب، فكل أحد يؤخذ بذنبه

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r11.claim: The Prophet’s warning is for everyone, but those who fear God are singled out because they accept and benefit from it.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r11.anchor: إنما تنذر أي: تخوف، يعني بهذا الذين يخشون يخافون ربهم إنما خصهم لقبولهم وانتفاعهم به وإلا فهو منذر للجميع

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r12.claim: One explanation is that they fear God in private, away from people, and in their inward selves.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r12.anchor: قيل: في خلواتهم وغيبتهم عن الخلق وسرائرهم

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r13.claim: Another explanation is that they believe in the unseen afterlife and its terrors.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r13.anchor: وقيل: في تصديقهم بالآخرة وأهوالها؛ لأنها غائبة عنهم

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r14.claim: A third explanation is that they fear God without seeing Him, since He is unseen to them.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r14.anchor: وقيل: يخافونه من غير أن يشاهدوه، فكأنه غائب عنهم

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r15.claim: The believers regularly maintain the prayer.

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r16.claim: One explanation of purification is cleansing oneself of sins; another is becoming upright and doing good.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r16.anchor: ومن تزكى قيل: تطهر من الآثام، وقيل: صلح وعمل خيرا

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r17.claim: The person who purifies himself benefits himself, since his reward reaches him.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r17.anchor: فإنما يتزكى لنفسه؛ لأن جزاءه يصل إليه

JISHUMI:v8p5840/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r18.claim: The return is to the place of God’s judgment, where recompense is given.
JISHUMI:v8p5840/r18.anchor: وإلى الله إلى موضع حكمه المصير أي: المرجع للجزاء

JISHUMI:v8p5843/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r1.claim: The passage shows that faith without performing prayer does not benefit a person, refuting the Murjiʾa.
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r1.anchor: وتدل أنه لا ينفع الإيمان من غير أداء الصلاة، فيبطل قول المرجئة

JISHUMI:v8p5843/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r2.claim: “Whoever purifies himself” shows that reward and punishment are recompense for deeds, refuting the Mujbira.
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r2.anchor: ويدل قوله: (ومن تزكى) أن الثواب والعقاب جزاء الأعمال، فيبطل قول المجبرة

JISHUMI:v8p5843/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r3.claim: The deeds belong to human agents, refuting the claim that they are created acts.
JISHUMI:v8p5843/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن ذلك فعلهم، فيبطل قولهم في المخلوق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r1.claim: Wizr and wiqr are synonyms; the verb means to carry a burden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r1.anchor: الوزر والوقر : أخوان ؛ ووزر الشيء إذا حمله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r2.claim: At Resurrection each soul bears its own sin; nobody is punished for another’s, unlike worldly tyrants who punish one for another’s wrongdoing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r2.anchor: والمعنى : أن كل نفس يوم القيامة لا تحمل إلا وزرها الذي اقترفته : لا تؤخذ نفس بذنب نفس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r3.claim: The feminine “burden-bearing” describes souls themselves: each burdened soul is found carrying its own, never another’s burden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r3.anchor: لأن المعنى أن النفوس الوازرات لا ترى منهن واحدة إلا حاملة وزرها ، لا وزر غيرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r4.claim: The misleaders’ additional burdens are their own sins of leading others astray, not other people’s sins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r4.anchor: تلك الآية في الضالين المضلين ، وأنهم يحملون أثقال إضلال الناس مع أثقال ضلالهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r5.claim: God refutes the misleaders’ promise to carry followers’ sins by saying they will carry none of those sins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r5.anchor: كذبهم الله تعالى في قولهم : { اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم } ( العنكبوت : 12 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r6.claim: The first clause establishes divine justice in not punishing without personal sin; the next says no one relieves a burdened soul who begs for help.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r6.anchor: الأول في الدلالة على عدل الله تعالى في حكمه ، وأنه تعالى لا يؤاخذ نفسا بغير ذنبها ، والثاني : في أن لا غياث يومئذ لمن استغاث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r7.claim: Even a close relative—father, child, or brother—will not answer a burdened soul’s plea to carry part of its load.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r7.anchor: وإن كان المدعو بعض قرابتها من أب أو ولد أو أخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r8.claim: The deficient verb’s implied subject is the person summoned, understood from the burdened soul’s call; omitting that person includes every possible summoned person.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r8.anchor: إلى المدعو المفهوم من قوله : { وإن تدع مثقلة }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r9.claim: This is a distributive generalization: not all summoned people can be relatives, but each possible person is covered in turn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r9.anchor: هو من العموم الكائن على طريق البدل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r10.claim: A variant reads dhū in the nominative and kāna as a complete verb, like the verse about a debtor in hardship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r10.anchor: ما تقول فيمن قرأ : ( ولو كان ذو قربى ) على كان التامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r11.claim: The incomplete kāna fits better: even if the person called were a relative; the complete verb would disrupt the passage’s cohesion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r11.anchor: نظم الكلام أحسن ملاءمة للناقصة ؛ لأن المعنى على أن المثقلة إن دعت أحدا إلى حملها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r12.claim: “In the unseen” can describe people fearing while unseen from punishment, or punishment unseen from them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r12.anchor: بالغيب } حال من الفاعل أو المفعول ، أي : يخشون ربهم غائبين عن عذابه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r13.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r13.claim: Another interpretation takes “in the unseen” to mean privately or secretly.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r14.claim: This describes the Prophet’s Companions, who habitually feared God and established prayer as an enduring landmark and raised standard.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r14.anchor: وهذه صفة الذين كانوا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أصحابه ، فكانت عادتهم المستمرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r15.claim: The Prophet can warn and benefit receptive people, unlike rebellious and obstinate opponents.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r15.anchor: إنما تقدر على إنذار هؤلاء وتحذيرهم من قومك ، وعلى تحصيل منفعة الإنذار فيهم دون متمرديهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r16.claim: Purification means acts of obedience and leaving sins; fear and prayer are part of purification.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r16.anchor: ومن تزكى } ومن تطهر بفعل الطاعات وترك المعاصي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r17.claim: A variant reads “whoever is more purified, purifies himself.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r18.claim: The return to God promises reward for those who purify themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r18.anchor: وإلى الله المصير } وعد للمتزكين بالثواب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r19.claim: After threatening opponents with removal, the passage describes the Resurrection’s terrors and then says only certain people benefit from warning; Muhammad may have warned them without effect before God disclosed their condition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r19.anchor: لما غضب عليهم في قوله : { إن يشأ يذهبكم } أتبعه الإنذار بيوم القيامة وذكر أهوالها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r20.claim: Alternatively, Muhammad warned of the Resurrection’s terrors without benefit, so God told him who would benefit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p616/r20.anchor: أو أخبره الله تعالى بعلمه فيهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r1.claim: No soul bears another soul's sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r1.anchor: أي لا تحمل نفس ما تحمله نفس أخرى من ذنوبها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r2.claim: وزير is related because a minister bears the ruler's burdens through administration.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r2.anchor: ومنه الوزير لأنه يحمل أثقال الملك بتدبيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says it means weighed down by sins.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r4.claim: On Judgment Day a sin-burdened soul may seek a bearer, but none will carry its sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r4.anchor: أن النفس التي قد أثقلتها ذنوبها إذا دعت يوم القيامة من يتحمل الذنوب عنها لم تجد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r5.claim: Even a close relative cannot accept the burden under the preceding rule.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r5.anchor: ولو كان المدعو إلى التحمل قريبا مناسبا , ولو تحمله عنها ما قبل تحمله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r6.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r6.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says they fear God privately, where no one sees them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r6.anchor: في السر حيث لا يطلع عليه أحد , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r7.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r7.claim: Ibn Isa interprets this as belief in the Hereafter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r7.anchor: في التصديق بالآخرة , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r8.claim: A further possibility is inward fear in the heart as well as fear in outward actions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p467#2/r8.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : يخشونه في ضمائر القلوب كما يخشونه في ظواهر الأفعال

MUJAHID:v2p531#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p531#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p531#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says that no one carries any part of another's burden, as in the verse's statement that no bearer bears another's load.
MUJAHID:v2p531#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وإن تدع مثقلة ﴾ [ أي مثقلة ذنوبا ] ( 1 ) ﴿ إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r1.claim: No sinful soul bears another's sin; each carries only what it earned and is not punished for another's deed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r1.anchor: ولا تحمل نفس آثمة اثم نفس أخرى والوزر والوقر اخوان ووزر الشىء إذا حمله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r2.claim: Wizr and wiqr are synonyms for burden; wazira describes the soul that carries it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r2.anchor: والوزر والوقر اخوان ووزر الشىء إذا حمله والوازرة صفة للنفس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r3.claim: Wazira is used instead of the generic soul because every sin-bearing soul carries its own burden, never another's.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r3.anchor: وإنما قيل وازرة ولم يقل ولا تزر نفس وزر آخرى لأن المعنى ان النفوس الوازرات لا ترى منهن واحدة إلا حاملة وزرها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r4.claim: Misleaders bear the burden of misleading others along with their own, but these are their own sins; scripture denies their claim to carry others' sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r4.anchor: ليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وارد فى الضالين المضلين فانهم يحملون أثقال اضلال الناس مع أثقال ضلالهم وذلك كله أوزارهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r5.claim: A soul weighed with sins may call someone to take part of its burden, but none will carry any of it for her.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r6.claim: The one summoned is understood as the subject of if he were a close relative; examples are a parent, child, or sibling.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r6.anchor: ذا قرابة قريبة كأب أو ولد أو أخ

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r7.claim: The first clause shows God's justice; the second says no one brings relief to a soul seeking help on that day.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r7.anchor: ان الأول دال على عدل الله فى حكمه وان لا يؤاخذ نفسا بغير ذنبها والثانى فى بيان أنه لا غياث يومئذ لمن استغاث

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r8.claim: Warning benefits those who fear their Lord: they may fear Him unseen from punishment, fear punishment while it is unseen to them, or fear in private.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r9.claim: Bil-ghayb can be circumstantial of either the subject who fears or the object of fear.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r9.anchor: حال من الفاعل أو المفعول أى يخشون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r10.claim: They establish prayer at its appointed times.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r10.anchor: ﴿ وأقاموا الصلاة ﴾ فى مواقيتها ﴿ ومن تزكى ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r11.claim: Tazakka means purification through acts of obedience and leaving sins; this benefits only the person purifying himself.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p340#3/r12.claim: The return is to God, a promise of reward for the one who purifies himself.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r1.speaker: author
