QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r1.claim: The commentary says this verse was treated earlier and is detached from what immediately precedes it.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r1.anchor: تقدم الكلام فيه، وهو مقطوع مما قبله

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r2.claim: The underlying form is tawzar; its wāw was deleted to match the form of yazir.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r3.claim: Wāzirah is an adjective of an elided noun, meaning a burden-bearing soul.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ supplies an elided nafs or beast for muthqalah and says the expression applies to masculine or feminine.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: أي نفس مثقلة أو دابة

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r5.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash understands a sin-burdened person to be asking another person to carry her sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r5.anchor: قال الأخفش: أي وإن تدع مثقلة إنسانا إلى حملها

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r6.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r6.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says ḥaml for what is carried on the back, pregnancy, and a date cluster is pronounced with fatḥah only.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r7.speaker: ابن السكيت
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit allows the word for a date cluster to be pronounced with either fatḥah or kasrah.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r7.anchor: وحكى ابن السكيت أن حمل النخلة يفتح ويكسر

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r8.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r8.claim: On al-Akhfash's parse, the omitted subject is the person being called upon: even if that person were a close relative, no burden would be carried.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r8.anchor: التقدير على قول الأخفش: ولو كان الإنسان المدعو ذا قربى

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r9.speaker: الفراء وسيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r9.claim: Al-Farraʾ permits the nominative dhū qurbā; Sibawayh accepts it as in 2:280, with kāna meaning ‘occurred’ or with a predicate understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r9.anchor:
وأجاز الفراء ولو كان ذو قربى. وهذا جائز عند سيبويه، ومثله
وإن كان ذو عسرة

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r10.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r10.claim: Sibawayh gives the elliptical example ‘people are requited for their deeds, if good then good,’ with a second case-form alternative.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r10.anchor: وحكى سيبويه: الناس مجزيون بأعمالهم إن خير فخير

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r11.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r11.claim: Ikrima relays that at the Resurrection a Jew or Christian asks a Muslim to help because of past kindness; the Muslim asks God until some punishment is reduced.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r11.anchor: وروي عن عكرمة أنه قال: بلغني أن اليهودي والنصراني يرى الرجل المسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r12.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r12.claim: Ikrima's report continues with parents, children, and spouses refusing requests to transfer a good deed or bear a sin because they fear their own judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r12.anchor: وأن الرجل ليأتي إلى أبيه يوم القيامة فيقول: ألم أكن بك بارا

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r13.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r13.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad pictures a mother reminding her child of pregnancy, nursing, and care, then asking him to carry one sin; he refuses, occupied with his own sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r13.anchor: فتقول: يا ولدي، ألم يكن بطني لك وعاء، ألم يكن ثديي لك سقاء

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r14.claim: The warning is accepted by those who fear God's punishment, as in the verse about those who follow the Reminder and fear the Merciful unseen.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18/r14.anchor: أي إنما يقبل إنذارك من يخشى عقاب الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r1.claim: Whoever purifies himself is guided for his own benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r1.anchor: أي من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r2.claim: A variant reads man izzakkā fa-innamā yazzakkā li-nafsih, using forms of purifying oneself.

QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:35:18#2/r3.anchor: وإلى الله المصير } أي إليه مرجع جميع الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r1.claim: After clear proofs, the point invites reflection: a lying Prophet would fear his own sin, which no one else can bear, and God does not need human worship; if people stray, no one carries their burden.
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r1.anchor: لما بين الحق بالدلائل الظاهرة والبراهين الباهرة ذكر ما يدعوهم إلى النظر فيه

RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r2.claim: No soul bears another’s sin, unlike the claim that others can say, “Follow our path and we will carry your sins.”
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r2.anchor: وليس كما يقول : { ءامنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم }

RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r3.claim: “A burden-bearing one” means a soul bearing sin; omitting an explicit noun is clear because the descriptive quality is inseparable from its subject.
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r3.anchor: أي نفس وازرة ولم يقل ولا تزر نفس وزر أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r4.claim: Saying “no burden-bearing one” makes clear that each soul bears its own burden but not another’s; simply saying “no soul bears another’s burden” could also include someone who bears no burden at all.
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r4.anchor: بين أنها تزر وزرها ولا تزر وزر الغير

RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r5.claim: The wording denies help both unsolicited and after a request: a needy person may endure quietly until the burden becomes so great that they ask.
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أن أحدا لا يحمل عن أحد شيئا مبتدئا ولا بعد السؤال ، فإن المحتاج قد يصبر

RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r6.claim: Calling the soul heavily burdened rules out lack of compassion as the reason no one helps: the load is severe, yet none of it is carried by another.
RAZI-FULL:v26p13#4/r6.anchor: يعني ليس عدم الوزر لعدم كونه محلا للرحمة بالثقل بل لكون النفس مثقلة ولا يحمل منها شيء

RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r1.claim: Even a close relative will not carry the burden: the sinner may be able to bear it, the other is heavily burdened, the request invites mercy, and kinship invites help, yet each remains under their own load.
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r1.anchor: أي يحصل جميع المعاني الداعية إلى الحمل من كون النفس وازرة قوية تحتمل وكون الأخرى مثقلة

RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r2.claim: The Prophet has already brought all possible guidance; warning benefits only those whose hearts are filled with awe and whose outward lives show worship.
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r2.anchor: فلا تنذر إنذارا مفيدا إلا الذين تمتلىء قلوبهم خشية وتتحلى ظواهرهم بالعبادة

RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r3.claim: Fear of God describes the inward act, while establishing prayer describes outward action, parallel to the pairing of faith with righteous deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r3.anchor: في ذلك المعنى ، ثم لما بين

RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r4.claim: After stating that no one bears another’s burden, the passage adds that purification benefits the person who purifies themself.

RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r5.claim: If purification’s benefit or sin’s consequence is not visible in this life, both will become apparent in the afterlife when all return to God.
RAZI-FULL:v26p14/r5.anchor: إن لم تظهر فائدته عاجلا فالمصير إلى الله يظهر عنده في يوم اللقاء في دار البقاء

STUDYQURAN:35:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r1.speaker: Aj, IK, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r1.claim: Aj, IK, R, and Ṭ explain that no one bears another person’s sins or duties.
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r1.anchor: no one will bear the sins or duties of others (Aj, IK, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:35:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r2.claim: Aj reads the rule that each bears their own burden as a manifestation of God’s Justice.

STUDYQURAN:35:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r3.claim: Q understands the phrase as opening a new discussion.
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r3.anchor: the introduction of a new discussion (Q)

STUDYQURAN:35:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r4.claim: R connects it to the prior description of human poverty before God: people cannot assume or transfer burdens because they lack power to decide such matters.
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r4.anchor: one cannot take on the burden of another or cast one’s burden upon another (R)

STUDYQURAN:35:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r5.speaker: Commentators
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r5.claim: Commentators reconcile 29:13 by taking leaders’ own burdens as the consequences of their own being misled, and others’ burdens as the consequences of misleading them.
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r5.anchor: Commentators reconcile this phrase with 29:13, Surely they will bear their own burdens

STUDYQURAN:35:18/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r6.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r6.claim: IK explains that whoever does good deeds receives their benefit.
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r6.anchor: whoever performs good deeds receives the benefit of those deeds (IK)

STUDYQURAN:35:18/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r7.claim: The verse presents moral reflexivity: good and evil actions ultimately affect the person who performs them.
STUDYQURAN:35:18/r7.anchor: This verse thus demonstrates a moral reflexivity in which the ultimate impact of actions, good or bad, is always upon the one who performs

QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r2.claim: Each person answers for their own deeds and record, and has an individual relation with God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r2.anchor: كل مطالب بعمله ، وكل محاسب عن ديوانه

QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r3.claim: Proxy applies to some worship but not gnosis; even thousands of saints cannot make up a sinner's missed prayer unless the sinner performs it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r3.anchor: ومن العبادات ما تجري فيه النيابة ولكن في المعارف لا تجري النيابة

QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r4.claim: Divine reproach and address are personal: no one else hears the address meant for the servant, whose place in God's heart is preserved.
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r4.anchor: فعتابك لا يجري مع غيرك والخطاب الذي معك لا يسمعه غيرك

QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r5.claim: Warning is alerting someone to danger and khashya is fear; warning benefits only those who have fear, like creatures gathering with their own kind.

TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r1.claim: No sinner bears another person's sin.
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r1.anchor: يكون عليه وزر لا يجد أحدا يحمل عنه من وزره شيئا

TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r2.claim: A burdened person who asks another to carry her sins finds no bearer, even when the person asked is a close relative such as a father or brother.
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r2.anchor: سألته ذا قرابة من أب أو أخ وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a burdened person finds no one to carry any of their sin.
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى} [فاطر: 18]

TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says this appeal repeats the meaning that no soul bears another's burden.
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء} [فاطر: 18] كنحو: {لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى}

TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r5.claim: Qatada explains the burden as sins; even close relatives carry none, and no one bears another's sins.
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها} [فاطر: 18] " إلى ذنوبها

TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r6.claim: ذا قربى is the predicate completing kāna: the person asked to carry the sins is a close relative.
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r6.anchor: ونصب ذا قربى على تمام كان لأن معنى الكلام: ولو كان الذي تسأله أن يحمل عنها ذنوبها ذا قربى لها

TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r7.claim: مثقلة is feminine because the wording implies nafs, feminine for both men and women, as in 3:185.
TAB-FULL:v19p353#2/r7.anchor: وأنثت مثقلة، لأنه ذهب بالكلام إلى النفس، كأنه قيل: وإن تدع نفس مثقلة من الذنوب إلى حمل ذنوبها

TAB-FULL:v19p355/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p355/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p355/r1.claim: The warning benefits those who fear God's punishment on the Resurrection without seeing it, because they believe the message and the Messenger; sealed hearts do not benefit.
TAB-FULL:v19p355/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب} [فاطر: 18] «أي يخشون النار»

TAB-FULL:v19p355/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p355/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p355/r2.claim: Qatada glosses fearing their Lord as fearing the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v19p355/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب} [فاطر: 18] «أي يخشون النار»

TAB-FULL:v19p356/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p356/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p356/r1.claim: Purification means turning from disbelief and sins through repentance, faith, and obedience; its reward is God's pleasure, Paradise, and escape from punishment.
TAB-FULL:v19p356/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه} [فاطر: 18] «أي من يعمل صالحا فإنما يعمله لنفسه»

TAB-FULL:v19p356/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p356/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p356/r2.claim: Qatada says whoever does good deeds does so for their own benefit.
TAB-FULL:v19p356/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه} [فاطر: 18] «أي من يعمل صالحا فإنما يعمله لنفسه»

TABATABAI:35:18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18/r1.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:35:18/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes wazr as refuge (with fatḥa) from wizr as burden (with kasra and sukūn); burden metaphorically denotes sin, as in the cited verses.
TABATABAI:35:18/r1.anchor: قال الراغب الوزر - بفتحتين - الملجأ الذي يلتجأ إليه من الجبل

TABATABAI:35:18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18/r2.claim: No soul bearing sin carries another soul’s sin; each is answerable only for the sin it itself acquired.
TABATABAI:35:18/r2.anchor: ولا تحمل نفس حمل غيرها الذي أثقلها وإن كانت ذات قربى

TABATABAI:35:18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18/r3.claim: The verse answers an implied objection to the preceding threat of replacement and destruction: believers will not be punished for the disbelievers’ sins.
TABATABAI:35:18/r3.anchor: قيل هؤلاء المكذبون أخذوا بوزرهم فما حال المؤمنين؟ أيؤخذون بوزر غيرهم؟

TABATABAI:35:18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18/r4.claim: A sin-burdened soul’s plea for someone else to carry its burden is refused, even if the person asked is a close relative such as a parent, sibling, or sister.
TABATABAI:35:18/r4.anchor: لا يستجاب لها ولا يحمل من حملها شيء ولو كان المدعو ذا قربى للداعي

TABATABAI:35:18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18/r5.claim: The disbelievers with sealed hearts do not benefit from warning; its effective recipients are those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer, believing and worshipping God.
TABATABAI:35:18/r5.anchor: هؤلاء المكذبون لا ينتفعون بالإنذار ولا تتحقق معهم حقيقة الإنذار لأنهم مطبوع على قلوبهم

TABATABAI:35:18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18/r6.claim: The recipients fear God and pray in response to the warning, not beforehand; otherwise warning would redundantly follow an already achieved result. Prayer is the best and most important worship.
TABATABAI:35:18/r6.anchor: يخشون ربهم بالغيب ويقيمون الصلاة إثر إنذارك لا أنهم يخشون ربهم ويصلون ثم ينذرون بعد ذلك

TABATABAI:35:18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18/r7.claim: The contrast between those who benefit from warning and the deniers anticipates the following comparisons of blind and sighted, darkness and light, shade and heat, and living and dead.
TABATABAI:35:18/r7.anchor: الفريقان لا يستويان لأن مثلهم مثل الأعمى والبصير، والظلمات والنور، والظل والحرور، والأحياء والأموات

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r1.claim: The preceding discussion compares the timing of warning and response to the wording of Joseph’s statement in 12:36.

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r2.claim: Purification replaces the mention of fear and prayer to show that the aim of preaching and warning is purification of the soul, which takes the form of fearing God unseen and praying.
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r2.anchor: المطلوب بالدعوة والإنذار هو التزكي وتزكية النفس تلبسها بالخشية من الله على الغيب وإقامة الصلاة

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r3.claim: The statement confirms God’s self-sufficiency: purification benefits the person who purifies themself, not God.
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r3.anchor: فهو تعالى لا ينتفع بما يدعو إليه من التزكي بل الذي تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفع نفسه

TABATABAI:35:18-22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r4.claim: Purification is not wasted: both groups inevitably return to God for judgment and recompense, and the purified receive the finest reward.
TABATABAI:35:18-22/r4.anchor: فإن كلا من الفريقين صائرون إلى ربهم لا محالة وهو يحاسبهم ويجازيهم

AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r1.claim: ذا قربى is predicative in the clause, which explains the wording ولو كان.
AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r1.anchor: وقال {ولو كان ذا قربى} لأنه خبر

AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r2.claim: The clause means if a burdened person calls another person to carry her load, none of it will be borne for her, even by a relative.
AKHFASH:v2p485#2/r2.anchor: فكأنه قال و"إن تدع إنسانا لا يحمل من ثقلها شيئا ولو كان الانسان ذا قربى

TABRISI:35:18-22/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r4.claim: God’s judgment is just: no soul bears another soul’s sin, and each is answerable for the wrong it commits.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r4.anchor: أي لا تحمل نفس حاملة حمل نفس أخرى أي لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره وإنما يؤاخذ كل بما يقترفه

TABRISI:35:18-22/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r5.claim: Even if a soul weighed down by sins asks another to carry some of its burden, that other bears nothing, even if closely related.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r5.anchor: أي وأن تدع نفس مثقلة بالآثام غيرها الى أن يتحمل عنها شيئا من إثمها

TABRISI:35:18-22/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:35:18-22/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas pictures a father or mother asking a child to carry a burden; the child replies that his own burden is enough.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس يقول الأب والأم يا بني احمل عني فيقول حسبي ما علي

TABRISI:35:18-22/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r7.claim: The people who fear their Lord while absent from the judgments and terrors of the afterlife are the ones who benefit from warning; warning has no effect on others.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r7.anchor: أي وهم غائبون عن أحكام الآخرة وأهوالها وهذا كقوله إنما أنت منذر من يخشاها

TABRISI:35:18-22/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:35:18-22/r8.claim: Another explanation is that they fear their Lord in private, away from other people.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r8.anchor: وقيل: الذين يخشون ربهم في خلواتهم وغيبتهم عن الخلق

TABRISI:35:18-22/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r9.claim: They maintain prayer and observe its conditions.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r9.anchor: أداموها وقاموا بشرائطها وإنما عطف الماضي

TABRISI:35:18-22/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r10.claim: The past tense for establishing prayer alongside the present tense for fearing signals that fear is constant whereas prayer has appointed times.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r10.anchor: وإنما عطف الماضي على المستقبل إشعارا باختلاف المعنى لأن الخشية لازمة في كل وقت

TABRISI:35:18-22/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r11.claim: Tazakka means performing obedience and fulfilling zakat and other duties.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r11.anchor: أي فعل الطاعات وقام بما يجب عليه من الزكاة وغيرها من الواجبات

TABRISI:35:18-22/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:35:18-22/r12.claim: Another interpretation is purification from sins.

TABRISI:35:18-22/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r13.claim: The benefit and reward of purification return to the person who purifies himself, not someone else.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r13.anchor: لأن جزاء ذلك يصل إليه دون غيره

TABRISI:35:18-22/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:35:18-22/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:35:18-22/r14.claim: All creatures return to God, the sole judge, who rewards each according to his deeds.
TABRISI:35:18-22/r14.anchor: أي مرجع الخلق كلهم إلى حيث لا يملك الحكم إلا الله سبحانه فيجازي كلا على قدر عمله

THALABI:v8p104#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p104#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p104#2/r1.claim: No soul burdened by sins can transfer any of its burden to another, even a close relative such as a child, parent, or sibling.
THALABI:v8p104#2/r1.anchor: وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه يعني وإن تدع نفس مثقلة بذنوب غيرها

THALABI:v8p104#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p104#2/r2.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
THALABI:v8p104#2/r2.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad pictures a mother asking her son on Judgment Day to carry one sin; he refuses, saying he is occupied with his own fate.
THALABI:v8p104#2/r2.anchor: سمعت الفضيل بن عياض يقول: قوله سبحانه: لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى قال: يعني الوالدة تلقي ولدها يوم القيامة

THALABI:v8p104#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p104#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p104#2/r3.claim: Those who fear their Lord unseen fear Him without having seen Him; whoever purifies himself benefits himself, and all return to God.
THALABI:v8p104#2/r3.anchor: إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب أي يخافونه ولم يروه، وأقاموا الصلاة ومن تزكى صلح عمل خيرا وصالحا فإنما يتزكى لنفسه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p360#9/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p360#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p360#9/r1.claim: A soul burdened with sins cannot get another to carry any of its burden, even if the person it calls is a close relative.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p360#9/r1.anchor: وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء} يقول: إن دعت نفس ذات ذنوب قد أثقلتها ذنوبها ليحمل عنها شيء منها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the phrase as a soul burdened with sins calling for help with its burden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج: أي وإن تدع نفس مثقلة بالذنوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj likewise explains it as a soul weighed down by sins calling for help.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r3.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج: أي وإن تدع نفس مثقلة بالذنوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says nafs is grammatically used for either a male or a female, as in “Every soul tastes death” (3:185).
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p413#2/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: (والنفس تعبر عن الذكر والأنثى، كقوله (¬1): {كل نفس ذائقة الموت}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r1.claim: The burden is the sins and transgressions carried by the soul.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r1.anchor: أي: ما حمل من الخطايا والذنوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r2.claim: The pronoun in “none of it will be carried” refers to that soul’s burden.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r3.claim: Muqātil says even a close relation carries none of another person’s sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: ولو كان بينهما ما حملت عنها شيء من وزرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās pictures the burdened person asking her son to carry some of her load, while he replies that he has enough of his own.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يقول: يا بني احمل عني، فيقول: حسبي ما علي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the close relation can be a father, son, or someone similar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي ولو كان الذي يدعوه ذا قربى، مثل الأب والابن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these are God’s allies, who fear Him and fear His punishment though it is unseen to them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r7.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the warning benefits only those who fear their Lord; it is as though the Prophet warns them rather than those whom warning cannot benefit, as in 79:45.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p414#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: تأويله أن إنذارك إنما ينفع الذين يخشون ربهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains purification as finding guidance, which benefits the person himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r2.claim: Muqātil explains it as becoming righteous; that righteousness benefits the person himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: من صلح فصلاحه لنفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p415/r3.claim: All return to God, who will recompense people for their deeds in the afterlife.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r1.claim: No soul bearing sin carries another soul's sin.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r1.anchor: لا تحمل نفس حاملة { وزر أخرى } حمل نفس أخرى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r2.claim: Even if a sin-laden person calls a close relative such as a father or son to carry the burden, none of it will be taken from that person.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r2.anchor: نفس مثقلة بالذنوب { إلى حملها } ذنوبها { لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان } المدعو { ذا قربى } مثل الأب والابن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r3.claim: The warning benefits those who fear God without having seen Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r3.anchor: إنما ينفع إنذارك الذين يخافون الله تعالى، ولم يروه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r4.claim: The person who purifies himself does good.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r4.anchor: لم يروه { ومن تزكى } عمل خيرا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r1.claim: The appeal is for someone to carry the burden away from the burdened person.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r2.claim: No relative can carry any of another relative’s sins.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r2.anchor: لا يحمل قريب عن قريبه شيئا من ذنوبه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r3.claim: The Prophet’s warning is accepted only by those who fear their Lord unseen.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r4.claim: Fearing God unseen means fearing Him privately, where no one can observe them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r4.anchor: في السر حيث لا يطلع عليهم أحد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r5.claim: The prayer they establish is the obligatory prayer.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r6.claim: Purifying oneself here means doing a righteous deed.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784/r7.claim: The one who purifies himself will find its reward.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r1.claim: The opening states individual responsibility, a standard for religious accountability and the Hereafter, and a legal maxim that influenced Muslim jurists from early times; Western law reached personal punishment only recently.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r1.anchor: İlk cümle sorumlulukla ilgili önemli bir ilkenin ifadesidir. Dinî sorumluluğun, kişinin âhirette vereceği hesabın temel ölçütlerinden birini ortaya koyan bu ifade aynı zamanda bir hukuk vecizesi niteliğindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r2.claim: Some Meccan polytheists imagined that, as in worldly life, patrons or relatives could intercede to save them in the afterlife; the second clause dismisses that hope.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r2.anchor: Kur’an’ın inmeye başladığı sıralarda Mekke toplumunda, suçlu, dost ve yakınları yardımıyla cezalandırılmaktan kurtulabiliyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r3.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r3.claim: Zamakhshari distinguishes the clauses: the first expresses God's justice in not charging anyone with another's sin, and the second denies rescue from one's own sin through another's help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r3.anchor: Zemahşerî, iki cümle arasındaki farkı belirtirken birincinin Allah’ın hükmündeki adaleti ve kimseyi kendi işlemediği bir günahtan dolayı sorumlu tutmayacağı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r4.claim: The verse says no one can take another's burden or free them from responsibility, even if the person wishes to do so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r4.anchor: âyetin hiçbir kimsenin kendisi istese dahi başkasının günahını üstlenmeye ve onu sorumluluktan kurtarmaya gücünün yetmeyeceğini bildirmesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r5.claim: Those who mislead bear both their own error and the burden of leading others astray, while the misled remain accountable for choosing evil; this is also stated in 29:13 and hadith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r5.anchor: Başkalarını saptıranların hem kendi sapkınlıklarının hem de onları kötü yola itmelerinin vebalini çekmeleri ise ayrı bir konudur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r6.claim: The verse can also be understood as rejecting the Christian doctrine of original sin in which Jesus pays for all humanity's sins through his life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r6.anchor: Öte yandan bu âyette, Hıristiyanlık’taki Hz. Îsâ’nın bütün insanlığın günahının kefâretini hayatıyla ödediğini ifade eden “aslî günah” telakkisinin reddedildiği de söylenebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r7.claim: Warning benefits sincere believers who, unseen, believe in God with full submission, avoid disobedience, and feel responsibility and concern before Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r7.anchor: Görmediği halde Allah’tan korkma yani O’na içtenlikle, tam bir teslimiyet içinde iman etme, O’na karşı gelmekten kaçınma

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r8.claim: The other defining trait is careful prayer: putting faith into practice and not neglecting duties of worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r8.anchor: Namazı özenle kılma yani imanını davranışlarına yansıtma, O’na kulluk görevlerini ihmal etmeme

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r9.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r9.claim: The warning can benefit only those who do not persist in false beliefs and conduct; the Prophet cannot change those who obstinately resist, nor is that his duty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r9.anchor: muhatapların kendi bâtıl inanç ve davranışlarında inat etmemesi olduğu (Zemahşerî, III, 273)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r10.claim: The usual explanation is that those who obey God's commands, avoid prohibitions, and do good works benefit themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:35:18/r10.anchor: Allah’ın buyruklarına uyup yasaklarından kaçınma çabası içinde olanların ve iyi işler yapanların bundan yine kendilerinin yararlanacakları şeklinde açıklanmıştır

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r1.claim: Bāqillānī explains هصرت as drew and bent.

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r2.claim: He calls بغصني دوحة strained, saying the wording should not have made the tree two.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r2.anchor: وقوله بغصني دوحة تعسف ولم يكن من سبيله أن يجعلها اثنين

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r3.claim: He judges the second hemistich better: its two familiar descriptions recur in poetry, but remain acceptable despite the repetition.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r3.anchor: والمصراع الثاني أصح وليس فيه شيء إلا ما يتكرر على ألسنة الناس من هاتين الصفتين

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r4.claim: مهفهفة means light or slender, rather than heavy.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r4.anchor: وأما معنى قوله مهفهفة أنها مخففة ليست مثقلة

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r5.claim: المفاضة describes a woman whose length is disproportionate.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r5.anchor: والمفاضة التي اضطرب طولها والبيت مع مخالفته في الطبع

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r6.claim: This poem departs from the preceding poems in taste, reaches for affected words, and awkwardly singles out the collarbones as luminous after describing all of her as white.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r6.anchor: وما فيه من الخلل من تخصيص الترائب بالضوء بعد ذكر جميعها بالبياض فليس بطائل

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r7.claim: In عن أسيل, عن means by or with; the poet intends a cheek that is not bulky.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r7.anchor: معنى قوله عن أسيل أي بأسيل وإنما يريد خدا ليس بكز

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r8.claim: Saying she turns away yet reveals her face is discordant: revealing the face belongs with intimacy, not turning away.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r8.anchor: وقوله تصد وتبدي عن أسيل متفاوت لأن الكشف عن الوجه مع الوصل دون الصد

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r9.claim: تتقي بناظرة is a fine phrase, but attaching it to generic wild animals is flawed; he should specify gazelles or oryx, since some wild animals have ugly eyes.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r9.anchor: وقوله تتقي بناظرة لفظة مليحة ولكن أضافها إلى ما نظم به كلامه وهو مختل

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r10.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r10.speaker: الأصمعي
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r10.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī’s reported explanation takes مطفل as mature rather than a young girl; Bāqillānī calls this strained and the added word useless on that reading.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r10.anchor: زيادة لا فائدة فيها على هذا التفسير الذي ذكره الأصمعي ولكن قد يحتمل عندي أن يفيد

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r11.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r11.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r11.claim: He suggests مطفل may instead mean she has children and looks at them tenderly, so her gaze conveys maternal affection; the connection is only middling.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r11.anchor: ولكن قد يحتمل عندي أن يفيد غير هذه الفائدة فيقال إنها إذا كانت مطفلا لحظت أطفالها بعين رقة

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r12.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r12.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r12.claim: In the second line, ليس بفاحش means not excessively long, and نصته means she raised it.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r12.anchor: وأما البيت الثاني فمعنى قوله ليس بفاحش أي ليس بفاحش الطول ومعنى قوله نصته رفعته

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r13.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r13.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r13.claim: Calling a neck not excessively long is an indecent expression in praise of necks.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r13.anchor: ومعنى قوله ليس بفاحش في مدح الأعناق كلام فاحش موضوع منه

BAQILLANI:v1p178/r14.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r14.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r14.claim: Arab poets describe necks with almost magical skill, so Bāqillānī questions why this poet chose that word instead of a better expression such as Abū Nuwās’s.
BAQILLANI:v1p178/r14.anchor: وإذا نظرت في أشعار العرب رأيت في وصف الأعناق ما يشبه السحر فكيف وقع على هذه الكلمة

BAQILLANI:v1p51/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p51/r8.speaker: قالوا
BAQILLANI:v1p51/r8.claim: They claim ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه follows the khafīf meter, like the cited poetic line كل يوم بشمسه وغد مثل أمسه.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r3.claim: إنما does more than make إن grammatically inoperative: إن عمرا جاءني does not convey that Amr, rather than Zayd, was the one who came.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r3.anchor: لو قلت : ما جاءني زيد ، وإن عمرا جاءني ؛ لم يعقل منه أنك أردت

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r4.claim: These restrictive formulations indirectly condemn those who lack understanding or reverence as irrational and effectively unreachable by warning, rather than merely identifying the audience.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p268/r4.anchor: المعنى على أن من لم تكن له هذه الخشية فهو كأنه ليس له أذن تسمع وقلب يعقل

THALABI:v8p104/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p104/r1.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v8p104/r1.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl reconciles the verses by saying no bearer willingly carries another’s sin, while disbelievers will carry their own burdens and added burdens unwillingly.
THALABI:v8p104/r1.anchor: سئل الحسين بن الفضل عن الجمع بين هذه الآية وبين قوله سبحانه وتعالى: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم فقال: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى طوعا وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم كرها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r9.claim: No person bears another person's sin.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r9.anchor: {ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى} [فاطر: 18] لا يحمل أحد ذنب آخر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r10.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r10.claim: Al-Suddī paraphrases it as no female bearer carrying the burden of another soul, which is equivalent in meaning.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r10.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني: لا تحمل حاملة ذنب نفس أخرى، وهو نحوه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r11.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r11.claim: Mujāhid, transmitting from his father, says the heavily burdened person is weighed down with sins.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p783/r11.anchor: تفسير مجاهد، عن أبيه قال: مثقلة، أي: من الذنوب

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r10.claim: As a reminder of God's justice, no soul bears another soul's burden of sin.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r10.anchor: hem vizr çeken bir nefis diğerinin vizrini çekmez.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r11.claim: Vizr means weight, heavy load, grave sin, or liability; here it means the weight of sin's punishment.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r11.anchor: “Vizr” ağırlık, ağır yük, ağır günah, vebâl demektir. Burada günahın cezâsının ağırlığı demektir.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r12.claim: Each person is accountable for their own sin; tyrants cannot impose another's guilt on them, as the proverb says each sheep hangs by its own leg.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r12.anchor: Herkes kendi günahından mes’ul olur, kendi günahının cezâsını çeker; nitekim “her koyun kendi bacağından asılır” deriz.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r13.claim: There is no conflict with 29:13: people who both stray and lead others astray bear both burdens because both are their own sins.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r13.anchor: buyurulmuş olması da buna münâfî değildir. Çünkü o hem dâll hem mudil olanlar hakkındadır.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r14.claim: He cites a hadith that one who introduces an evil practice bears its burden and the burdens of those who follow it; followers still bear their own sins.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r14.anchor: “her kim bir kötü âdet çıkarırsa ona hem onun vizri hem de onu işleyenlerin vizri vardır.”

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r15.claim: Someone who promises to bear another's sin and leads that person into wrongdoing does not save them: the misled and the misleader each face the penalty for their own act.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r15.anchor: birisi “şunu şöyle yap da günahı varsa benim boynuma olsun” diye kefalet ederek diğerini bir günaha sokarsa, o boynuna aldığı günahı çekmeyecek değildir.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r16.claim: The term describing the heavily burdened soul may hint at these attempts to have another carry one's sin.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r16.anchor: Şu مُثْقَلَةٌ tâbirinde bunlara bir işaret de var gibidir.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r17.claim: No part of another's burden can be taken up willingly or by force; Judgment Day permits neither ransom nor helpful intercession.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r17.anchor: Rızâ ve ihtiyar ile de yüklenilmez, cebren de yüklenilmez. Çünkü o kıyamet günü لَّا تَجْزِى نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r18.claim: Even a close relative cannot carry another's burden; humans should not betray their trust by misleading others or offering to take their sins.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r18.anchor: Gerekse bir yakını olsun yani çağıran veya çağırılan bir yakını bile olsa yine yüklenilmez, o hâlde Allah’ın emaneti gibi göklerin ve yerin çekemediği ağır bir yükü yüklenmiş olan insan bir de o emanete hıyanet ederek

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r19.claim: People should not follow those who tell them to act while claiming that any resulting sin will be on someone else's account.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r19.anchor: diğer birtakımı da öylelere uyup “günahı varsa filânın boynuna” diye kendini nâra yakmamalıdır.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r20.claim: Muhammad's warning benefits those who fear and revere their Lord while still unseen, before coming into His presence.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r20.anchor: Rablerine gaybda, yani henüz huzûruna varmadan gıyabda haşyet beslerler, Allah korkusu, Allah saygısını duyar

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r21.claim: They establish prayer properly, convinced that they will meet their Lord, as 2:46 says.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r21.anchor: Rablerinin huzûrunda likāsına ereceklerine kāni‘olarak kılarlar.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r22.claim: Whoever purifies himself is purified for his own benefit and spiritual flourishing.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r22.anchor: temizlenen de ancak kendisi için temizlenir, feyizlenir.

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r23.claim: People either bear sin or purify themselves through complete faith, virtuous character, and righteous deeds; purification benefits the person alone.
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r23.anchor: çekenler başkasının vizrini çekmeyeceği gibi, nefislerini îmân-ı kâmil ve ahlâk-ı fâzıla ve a‘mâl-i sâliha ile

ELMALILI:35:15-22/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:35:15-22/r24.claim: Everyone ultimately returns to God and receives the reward or punishment due to them.

BURHAN:v2p114/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r3.speaker: قالوا
BURHAN:v2p114/r3.claim: They say the purification phrase scans as a truncated khafif meter.
BURHAN:v2p114/r3.anchor: ﴿ ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه ﴾ قالوا هو مجزوء من الخفيف

BURHAN:v2p313/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p313/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p313/r3.claim: These restrictive statements indirectly reproach those who lack fear or understanding, portraying their stubbornness as if they had no hearing, heart, or reason.
BURHAN:v2p313/r3.anchor: المقصود التعريض بذم من ليست له هذه الخشية وان يعرف انه لفرط عناده كانه ليس له اذن تسمع ولا قلب يعقل

NAHHAS:v3p367/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p367/r12.claim: This clause is detached from what precedes; the original form had an initial wāw, deleted to match yaziru.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r12.anchor: مقطوع مما قبله والأصل توزر حذفت الواو اتباعا ليزر

NAHHAS:v3p367/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p367/r13.claim: Wāziran is an adjective for an omitted noun meaning a burden-bearing soul.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r13.anchor: ( وازرة ) نعت لمحذوف أي نفس وازرة

NAHHAS:v3p367/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r14.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p367/r14.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies an omitted nafs or dābba; the expression can apply to masculine or feminine.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r14.anchor: قال الفراء أي نفس مثقلة أو دابة قال وهذا يقع للمذكر والمؤنث

NAHHAS:v3p367/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r15.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v3p367/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies an omitted human being: if a burdened person calls another person.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r15.anchor: قال الأخفش أي وإن تدع مثقلة إنسانا

NAHHAS:v3p367/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p367/r16.claim: Ḥaml is a load carried on the back; al-Kisāʾī gives fatḥa alone for a woman's pregnancy and a palm's fruit, while Ibn al-Sikkīt allows either fatḥa or kasra for palm fruit.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r16.anchor: والحمل ما كان على الظهر وحمل المرأة وحمل النخلة حكاهما الكسائي بالفتح لا غير

NAHHAS:v3p367/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r17.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v3p367/r17.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies the omitted word al-insān: even if the person called were a close relative.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r17.anchor: التقدير على قول الأخفش ولو كان الإنسان المدعو ذا قربى

NAHHAS:v3p367/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r18.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p367/r18.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also permits the nominative form dhū qurba.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r18.anchor: وأجاز الفراء ( ولو كان ذو قربى )

NAHHAS:v3p367/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p367/r19.claim: The nominative construction is valid according to Sibawayh, as in wa-in kāna dhū ʿusra; kāna may mean occurred or have an omitted predicate, and Sibawayh's example about people being repaid good for good illustrates the two analyses.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r19.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا جائز عند سيبويه ومثله

NAHHAS:v3p367/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r20.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v3p367/r20.claim: ʿIkrima reports that a Jew or Christian may ask a Muslim on Judgment Day to repay a past kindness by taking some punishment or a sin; the Muslim refuses from fear, as do fathers, sons, and spouses when asked to bear one another's burdens.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r20.anchor: وحكى الحكم بن أبان عن عكرمة أنه قال بلغني أن اليهودي والنصراني يرى الرجل المسلم يوم القيامة

NAHHAS:v3p367/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p367/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p367/r21.claim: The Prophet warns all people, but the verse singles out those who fear their Lord because they are the ones who benefit from the warning.
NAHHAS:v3p367/r21.anchor: وهو ينذر الخلق كلهم فخص الذين يخشون ربهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r6.claim: A soul weighed down with sins may call someone to carry its burden, but none of its sins will be carried for it.
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r6.anchor: المعنى إن تدع نفس مثقلة بالذنوب إلى حملها، إلى ذنوبها، لا يحمل من ذنوبها شيء

ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r7.claim: Even a person called to bear the burden may be a close relative, such as a father or son.
ZAJJAJ:v4p266/r7.anchor: أي ولو كان الذي تدعوه ذا قربى مثل الأب والابن، ومن أشبه هؤلاء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r7.claim: This passage reassures the Prophet by identifying the kinds of people who will accept the call and those who will be deprived of it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p334/r7.anchor: an assurance is sounded to the Prophet (sws) by informing him what type of people will accept this call

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r3.claim: At the Judgment, each soul bears its own burden and no soul can carry another's.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r3.anchor: on that day no soul will bear the burden of another; on the contrary, each soul shall bear its own burden.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r4.claim: The noun qualified by muṯqalah is omitted; the full phrase would be nafsun muṯqalatun, a soul burdened by its sins.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r4.anchor: The noun qualified by the word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r5.claim: The governing noun before ḥaml is omitted, as is kāna's noun al-madʿū; Islahi says these omissions are common in classical Arabic.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r5.anchor: the mud@āf (governing noun) is suppressed before ْلِمَح

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r6.claim: A soul burdened by sins will find no one to share its load, not even its closest relative.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r6.anchor: it will find none to help it even if it invokes help from its closest relative.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r7.claim: The virtuous did not share the sinner's wrongdoing in the world, so they will not become companions in sin in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r7.anchor: if they did not accompany its sins in the previous world, why will they become its companions in the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r8.claim: Wrongdoers are themselves engulfed by their sins and therefore cannot help anyone else.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p344/r8.anchor: they themselves will be buried in their sins

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r1.claim: The verse assures the Prophet to warn people, but the warning benefits only those who use their faculties, fear their unseen Lord, and persevere in prayer; he should leave the others to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r1.anchor: his warning can only be effective on those who use their intellect and other faculties of cognizance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r2.claim: Prayer is mentioned because it is the foremost outward expression of faith and a sign of fearing God while unseen.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r2.anchor: adhering to the prayer is the foremost manifestation of faith and a symbol of God’s fear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r3.claim: Someone heedless of prayer is heedless of God, however strongly that person verbally claims faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r3.anchor: He who is heedless of the prayer is heedless of God even though he may make tall claims to faith by his tongue.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r4.claim: Those who seek to shed sin and purify themselves should be diligent in prayer instead of relying on false support.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r4.anchor: should be diligent and vigilant in the prayer instead of relying on false support.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r5.claim: Purification benefits the person who acquires it; God needs no worship or obedience, His servants need Him, and all return to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p345/r5.anchor: it is His servants who are in need, and everyone is set to return to Him alone.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r9.claim: No soul bearing sin can carry another soul's burden.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r10.claim: A “burdened” person is weighed down by sins; the burden is the sins she carries, and no one summoned can bear any of it, even a close relative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r10.anchor: أي: نفس مثقلة بذنوبها غيرها، {إلى حملها} أي: حمل ما عليه من الذنوب، {لا يحمل منه شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a father or mother asking a child to carry some of their sins, while the child replies that he cannot and must answer for his own burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يلقى الأب والأم ابنه فيقول: يا بني احمل عني بعض ذنوبي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r5.claim: No sinful soul carries another's sin; 29:13 does not contradict this, since misleaders carry their own sin of misleading in addition to their own misguidance, not someone else's burden.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r5.anchor: فإنهم يحملون أثقال إضلالهم مع أثقال ضلالهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r6.claim: A muthqala is a soul weighed down by sins.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r7.claim: No one accepts a share of another's burden: the verse denies that another's sin can be borne on a soul's behalf, just as it denies that the soul bears another's sin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r7.anchor: نفى أن يحمل عنها ذنبها كما نفى أن يحمل عليها ذنب غيرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r8.claim: The called-on helper is omitted because it is implied by in tadʿu; the reading dhū qurbā supplies an omitted predicate and is preferable to treating kāna as a complete verb, which does not fit the syntax.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r8.anchor: فأضمر المدعو لدلالة إن تدع عليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r9.claim: The warning benefits those who fear their Lord unseen: either they fear the absent punishment, fear while alone, or the punishment is absent from them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r9.anchor: غائبين عن عذابه، أو عن الناس في خلواتهم، أو غائبا عنهم عذابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r10.claim: Those who establish prayer, along with those who fear God, are the ones who benefit from warning; the differing verb forms reflect ongoing practice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r10.anchor: واختلاف الفعلين لما مر من الاستمرار

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r11.claim: To purify oneself is to cleanse oneself of the stain of sins; that purification benefits the person alone.

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r12.claim: Another reading is man azkā fa-innamā yazzakkā; the inserted clause reinforces that fear of God and establishing prayer are themselves forms of purification.
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r12.anchor: وقرىء «ومن أزكى فإنما يزكي» وهو اعتراض مؤكد

BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:35:15-18/r13.claim: Everyone returns to God, who recompenses them for their purification.

DURR-FULL:v7p14/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r10.speaker: عمرو بن الأحوص
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r10.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, the Prophet said that no wrongdoer bears the burden except against himself.
DURR-FULL:v7p14/r10.anchor: عن عمرو بن الأحوص أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: في حجة الوداع ألا لا يجني جان إلا على نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r11.claim: After the threat, the text reassures Muslims that those who do no wrong will not bear a wrongdoer’s punishment, as in the promise to save the God-fearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r11.anchor: فعقب بأن من لم يأت وزرا لا يناله جزاء الوازر في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r12.claim: It may also promise rescue from a worldly destruction that strikes the warned unbelievers, as at Badr; this special promise does not conflict with the warning that communal trials can affect the righteous too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r12.anchor: وقد يكون وعدا بالإنجاء من عذاب الدنيا إذا نزل بالمهددين الإذهاب والإهلاك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r13.claim: Umm Salama asked whether a community would perish while righteous people were among them; the Prophet answered yes if evil became widespread.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p286/r13.anchor: وما ورد في حديث أم سلمة قالت : ( يا رسول الله أنهلك وفينا الصالحون ؟ قال : نعم إذا كثر الخبث )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r4.claim: تزر means to carry, and وزر means a burden; the verse concerns sins, transgressions, and crimes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r4.anchor: وتزر معناه تحمل، والوزر الثقل، وهذه الآية في الذنوب والآثام والجرائم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r5.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r5.claim: Qatada, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid explain the verse as concerning sins, transgressions, and crimes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية في الذنوب والآثام والجرائم، قاله قتادة وابن عباس ومجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r6.claim: The occasion was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira telling believers to reject Muhammad while he would bear their burdens; God ruled that no one bears another's burden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r6.anchor: وسببها أن الوليد بن المغيرة قال لقوم من المؤمنين اكفروا بمحمد وعلي وزركم، فحكم الله تعالى بأنه لا يحملها أحد عن أحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r7.claim: A ruler may take a relative for another's crime when the relative aided, supported, knew of, or approved the criminal's act and thereby shares in it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r7.anchor: فإنما ذلك لأن المأخوذ ربما أعان المجرم بمؤازرة ومواصلة أو اطلاع على حاله وتقرير لها، فهو قد أخذ من الجرم بنصيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r8.claim: The added burdens in 29:13 are those of people whom the offenders led astray.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r8.anchor: وهذا هو المعنى في قوله تعالى وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم [العنكبوت: 13] لأنهم أغووهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r9.claim: The Prophet says whoever establishes a good practice receives its reward and the reward of later practitioners, while whoever establishes an evil practice bears its burden and theirs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r9.anchor: وهو معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم «من سن سنة حسنة فله أجرها وأجر من عمل بها إلى يوم القيامة بعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r10.claim: وازرة is feminine because the word is treated like نفس; مثقلة is formed on the same basis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r10.anchor: وأنثت وازرة لأنه ذهب بها مذهب النفس وعلى ذلك أجريت مثقلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r11.claim: حمل is a physical load carried on the back and is borrowed for abstract loads such as sins; acquisitions are similarly attributed to the hand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r11.anchor: ما كان على الظهر في الأجرام، ويستعار للمعاني كالذنوب ونحوها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r12.claim: The omitted subject of كان is الداعي: the sense is even if the caller were a close relative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r12.anchor: واسم كان مضمر تقديره ولو كان الداعي، ثم أخبر تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r13.claim: Only those who fear God benefit from the warning and receive knowledge, although the Prophet was sent to warn all people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r13.anchor: إنما ينذر أهل الخشية وهم الذين يمنحون العلم، أي إنما ينتفع بالإنذار هم وإلا فلنذارة جميع العالم بعثه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r14.claim: He takes بالغيب to mean that the Prophet is absent from them and communicates only a message.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r14.anchor: وقوله بالغيب أي وهو بحال غيبة عنهم إنما هي رسالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r15.claim: Prayer is singled out from the other deeds to draw attention to it and honor it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r15.anchor: ثم خصص من الأعمال إقامة الصلاة تنبيها عليها وتشريفا لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r16.claim: The verse urges purification by offering the strongest hope of reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r16.anchor: ثم حض على التزكي بأن رجى عليه غاية الترجية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r17.speaker: طلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r17.claim: Talha reads ومن أزكى فإنما يزكي instead of the usual wording.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r18.claim: The passage concludes by warning that the return is to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p434#3/r18.anchor: ثم توعد بعد ذلك بقوله وإلى الله المصير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r4.claim: At the Resurrection no soul can bear another's sins; even a close parent or child cannot relieve a burdened relative, since each is occupied with their own fate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r4.anchor: ولو كان قريبا إليها، حتى ولو كان أباها أو ابنها، كل مشغول بنفسه وحاله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim reports Ikrima's scene of a neighbor, disbeliever, parent, and spouse seeking help or a single good deed at Judgment; even loved ones fear for themselves, while a believer's intercession only lowers a disbeliever's place in Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p541#2/r5.anchor: عكرمة في قوله: {وإن تدع مثقلة إلى حملها} الآية، قال: هو الجار يتعلق بجاره يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v8p5839/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r4.claim: Wizr is a heavy load that weighs down the back; its plural is awzar, and sins are called burdens for their weight.
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r4.anchor: والوزر: الحمل الثقيل المثقل للظهر، وجمعه: أوزار، ومنه: (يحملون أوزارهم)

JISHUMI:v8p5839/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r5.claim: Atham are burdens because they weigh heavily on a person; awzar al-harb likewise burdens those who wage it.
JISHUMI:v8p5839/r5.anchor: والآثام: الأوزار لثقلها عليه، ومنه: أوزار الحرب لثقلها على أهلها

MUQATIL:35:15-19/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r4.claim: No soul bears another soul's sin; even a close relative cannot carry any of a burdened person's sins.
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r4.anchor: لا تحمل نفس خطيئة نفس أخرى { وإن تدع مثقلة } من الوزر { إلى حملها } من الخطايا أن يحمل عنها

MUQATIL:35:15-19/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r5.claim: The warning benefits believers who fear their Lord unseen, meaning they believe in Him without seeing Him.
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r5.anchor: { إنما تنذر } المؤمنين { الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب } آمنوا به ولم يروه

MUQATIL:35:15-19/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r6.claim: Establishing prayer means completing the obligatory prayer.

MUQATIL:35:15-19/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r7.claim: Whoever becomes righteous benefits himself; all return to God for recompense according to their deeds in the afterlife.
MUQATIL:35:15-19/r7.anchor: { ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه } ومن صلح فصلاحه لنفسه { وإلى الله المصير } [آية: 18] فيجزى بالأعمال في الأخرة
